Just this Wednesday I was on the air with Olivia from Tennessee Conservative News talking about how the death penalty doesn't apply to child rape if the child doesn't die -- that's the Supreme Court's rule, and fine, that's the law. But today the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals taught me something new: apparently the death penalty doesn't fully apply to murder either -- not when the method might scare the person being executed.
Because that's the only way to read what happened in Tennessee today. The penalty of death, we are now told, must be administered peacefully. Comfortably. Maybe with a conversation. Light a candle, burn some incense, hand out lilies, I guess -- regardless of how horribly the victim died. Crazy days.
Christa Pike killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995 -- a brutal, senseless murder committed when Pike herself was barely more than a teenager. It is incredibly rare for a woman to be sentenced to death in this country, so you know it was bad if she was going to die. Only 18 women have been executed in the modern death penalty era, which began in 1977. The most recent was Amber McLaughlin in Missouri in 2023 -- unlucky her, I guess, wrong circuit. 8th not 6th. Women account for 1% of all executions; men account for the other 1,664. Experts say that's because women commit fewer violent crimes. Fine.
Researchers have also found that 96% of women on death row were raped, sexually abused as children, or subjected to domestic violence before their arrest. I mention that because Pike's lawyers built a 226-page clemency petition on exactly that -- her age at the time of the crime, and the claim that her trial attorney never told the jury she was a victim of extensive child sexual abuse and multiple rapes.
And so we're clear about what kind of guest of the state we're talking about: while on death row, Pike tried to kill a fellow inmate with a shoelace. Not exactly time served with good behavior.
Now watch the dominoes fall. Less than a week before the execution, the Tennessee Supreme Court denied her request for a stay, finding she "failed to demonstrate a likelihood of success on the merits of her claims." Governor Bill Lee confirmed Monday he would not step in to keep Pike alive past her September 30 execution date. The U.S. Supreme Court denied her final stay request yesterday, September 29. So that should have been it. Last chance. But...
The Sixth Circuit issued a stay this morning, filed just before Pike's execution was scheduled to begin at 10 a.m. Quote the order: "The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee determined that it did not have jurisdiction over Christa Pike's Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b)(6) motion to reopen the judgment denying habeas relief... Therefore, it is ORDERED that execution of the sentence of death upon the movant is STAYED until further order of this court."
Read that again. Nobody ruled that her claims were good. Nobody ruled that she's innocent of the procedural mess. The court simply wasn't sure the lower court was *allowed* to say no -- so until they sort that out, no execution. Her lawyers called it the court "recognizing the serious concerns about Christa's scheduled execution." Mind you, this is the court whose territory is Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee -- 16 judges, based in Ohio -- and it found a reason that the Governor of Tennessee (state's rights) and the United States Supreme Court (federal, all nine) both passed on.
The "serious concerns" are the protocol arguments. In a hearing last month, Pike's team argued the state's execution protocols would make her death torturous because of her physical, medical, and psychological conditions, including PTSD. The state's answer: she'd be moved to Riverbend Maximum Security Institution 24 hours before, and the goal was that she'd be observed only by female corrections staff. Keep Riverbend in mind for a second.
Riverbend is where Tony Carruthers was supposed to be executed in May, until medical staff spent over an hour failing to establish IV access and the state gave up -- an attempted execution so botched it prompted a pause from Governor Lee. It's where Anthony Darrell Hines was put to death in August for the 1985 murder of Catherine Jean Jackson Jenkins -- so the machinery demonstrably worked a month ago. And the doctor involved in the Carruthers attempt, Mark Fowler, is the one overseeing Pike's. That's the thread the anti-death-penalty groups pulled, and they found a friendly hearing in the Sixth Circuit to buy her time that a Governor and the U.S. Supreme Court didn't deem worthy. (Very much like the mistrial that jury handed that Clancy woman who killed her kids. The court system is busted.)
Pike's letter from death row: "When my people showed up for me -- they have showed up and showed out! I am humbled beyond words." And this: "Whether my clemency is granted or not, I am at peace. I am not afraid to die. I am only nervous about the process."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dbe5a363-da0b-4a6f-98b1-f940fa1461eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There it is. Nervous about the process. Colleen Slemmer didn't get a process. She got thirty years of her mother waiting for justice.
There are currently 45 women on death row across the country, so at this rate we're going to see this four dozen more times. California has the most, 17 -- though Governor Gavin Newsom has ordered that no executions take place since 2019, so those ladies can relax. New York, 7, and Texas, 6, have executed the most women since 1900. Not a lot.
Slemmer's mother, after the stays started falling: "Maybe now finally we have justice. It may not bring my daughter back, but it might save another person from getting killed because she will do it again."
That was the whole point. Not the candle. Not the incense. Not the lilies. Somewhere tonight, lawyers are racing in front of sixteen judges in Ohio over whether a federal court was allowed to hear a motion -- so that a woman condemned for one of the ugliest murders in Tennessee history doesn't have to be nervous about the process. Her victim didn't even get a stay of the parking lot.

clean_body: until further order of this court | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? until further order of this court | | | Sep 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | Just this Wednesday I was on the air with Olivia from Tennessee Conservative News talking about how the death penalty doesn't apply to child rape if the child doesn't die -- that's the Supreme Court's rule, and fine, that's the law. But today the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals taught me something new: apparently the death penalty doesn't fully apply to murder either -- not when the method might scare the person being executed. Because that's the only way to read what happened in Tennessee today. The penalty of death, we are now told, must be administered peacefully. Comfortably. Maybe with a conversation. Light a candle, burn some incense, hand out lilies, I guess -- regardless of how horribly the victim died. Crazy days. Christa Pike killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995 -- a brutal, senseless murder committed when Pike herself was barely more than a teenager. It is incredibly rare for a woman to be sentenced to death in this country, so you know it was bad if she was going to die. Only 18 women have been executed in the modern death penalty era, which began in 1977. The most recent was Amber McLaughlin in Missouri in 2023 -- unlucky her, I guess, wrong circuit. 8th not 6th. Women account for 1% of all executions; men account for the other 1,664. Experts say that's because women commit fewer violent crimes. Fine. Researchers have also found that 96% of women on death row were raped, sexually abused as children, or subjected to domestic violence before their arrest. I mention that because Pike's lawyers built a 226-page clemency petition on exactly that -- her age at the time of the crime, and the claim that her trial attorney never told the jury she was a victim of extensive child sexual abuse and multiple rapes. And so we're clear about what kind of guest of the state we're talking about: while on death row, Pike tried to kill a fellow inmate with a shoelace. Not exactly time served with good behavior. Now watch the dominoes fall. Less than a week before the execution, the Tennessee Supreme Court denied her request for a stay, finding she "failed to demonstrate a likelihood of success on the merits of her claims." Governor Bill Lee confirmed Monday he would not step in to keep Pike alive past her September 30 execution date. The U.S. Supreme Court denied her final stay request yesterday, September 29. So that should have been it. Last chance. But... The Sixth Circuit issued a stay this morning, filed just before Pike's execution was scheduled to begin at 10 a.m. Quote the order: "The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee determined that it did not have jurisdiction over Christa Pike's Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b)(6) motion to reopen the judgment denying habeas relief... Therefore, it is ORDERED that execution of the sentence of death upon the movant is STAYED until further order of this court." Read that again. Nobody ruled that her claims were good. Nobody ruled that she's innocent of the procedural mess. The court simply wasn't sure the lower court was allowed to say no -- so until they sort that out, no execution. Her lawyers called it the court "recognizing the serious concerns about Christa's scheduled execution." Mind you, this is the court whose territory is Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee -- 16 judges, based in Ohio -- and it found a reason that the Governor of Tennessee (state's rights) and the United States Supreme Court (federal, all nine) both passed on. The "serious concerns" are the protocol arguments. In a hearing last month, Pike's team argued the state's execution protocols would make her death torturous because of her physical, medical, and psychological conditions, including PTSD. The state's answer: she'd be moved to Riverbend Maximum Security Institution 24 hours before, and the goal was that she'd be observed only by female corrections staff. Keep Riverbend in mind for a second. Riverbend is where Tony Carruthers was supposed to be executed in May, until medical staff spent over an hour failing to establish IV access and the state gave up -- an attempted execution so botched it prompted a pause from Governor Lee. It's where Anthony Darrell Hines was put to death in August for the 1985 murder of Catherine Jean Jackson Jenkins -- so the machinery demonstrably worked a month ago. And the doctor involved in the Carruthers attempt, Mark Fowler, is the one overseeing Pike's. That's the thread the anti-death-penalty groups pulled, and they found a friendly hearing in the Sixth Circuit to buy her time that a Governor and the U.S. Supreme Court didn't deem worthy. (Very much like the mistrial that jury handed that Clancy woman who killed her kids. The court system is busted.) Pike's letter from death row: "When my people showed up for me -- they have showed up and showed out! I am humbled beyond words." And this: "Whether my clemency is granted or not, I am at peace. I am not afraid to die. I am only nervous about the process." | | ---|---|--- There it is. Nervous about the process. Colleen Slemmer didn't get a process. She got thirty years of her mother waiting for justice. There are currently 45 women on death row across the country, so at this rate we're going to see this four dozen more times. California has the most, 17 -- though Governor Gavin Newsom has ordered that no executions take place since 2019, so those ladies can relax. New York, 7, and Texas, 6, have executed the most women since 1900. Not a lot. Slemmer's mother, after the stays started falling: "Maybe now finally we have justice. It may not bring my daughter back, but it might save another person from getting killed because she will do it again." That was the whole point. Not the candle. Not the incense. Not the lilies. Somewhere tonight, lawyers are racing in front of sixteen judges in Ohio over whether a federal court was allowed to hear a motion -- so that a woman condemned for one of the ugliest murders in Tennessee history doesn't have to be nervous about the process. Her victim didn't even get a stay of the parking lot. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. \- Status is live: The stay is "until further order of this court" -- the state can (and likely will) run back to the Sixth Circuit en banc or the Supreme Court within hours/days. as of this writing. \- The 96% abuse figure comes from research on women on death row -- (DPIC/researchers). | | Just three days into my first term in Congress, a violent mob attacked the Capitol.

**I didn't go to Congress to fight these partisan wars. That day made it clear to me that part of my job in Washington was going to be speaking up and speaking out when something is wrong.

I was elected to solve problems. To deliver for the people at home in the South Sound. That's exactly what I've done every day since.**

This administration has put the American people at war on many fronts: with each other, with our own institutions, and most recently, in a war with Iran that it can't explain.

I'll say it again: there's no exit strategy. Meanwhile, the economy is in the tank, costs keep climbing, and the President is banning news outlets because he needs a distraction.

I'm not waiting for things to get better on their own. My Fairness for Servicemembers and their Families Act is now law, so military death benefits keep pace with the cost of living. That matters in a district that's home to about 100,000 service members and military families at JBLM.

The last weeks of a campaign are a candidate's last chance to put their strongest message for our state in front of voters.
And Allison's opponent is continuing to spew lies about the integrity of our elections -- just as he's done since the start of this race.
Friend, from talking nonsense about removing our ballot boxes, to staying silent in the face of Trump's attacks to mail-in voting, to focusing on nonexistent problems with other states' elections, our opponent's finger-pointing should tell us everything about his vision for Ohio:
He simply doesn't have one.

subject: Before midnight, let’s have Rachel’s back
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Let’s show the strength behind our candidates and give them the resources to win.
#
Peter,
Tonight is our last public end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, and I’m asking you to stand with our endorsed candidate, Rachel Wallace, before we run out of time.
Rachel grew up in Pottsville, Pennsylvania, where her family has lived for 10 generations. She’s served at the State Department, in the Senate, and in the White House — then moved home when her mom was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
**Now she’s running for Congress to deliver for the community that raised her.**
**[Will you split a donation between Rachel’s campaign and Small Town PAC before midnight to help us put up strong public numbers and give her the resources to flip this district from red to blue?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260930-rw.zJJafi&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-1159&t=1&akid=1159%2E34582%2EuSJY0s)**
Rachel comes from a family of coal miners, farmers, union workers, and small business owners. She knows what it means to work hard and still feel like Washington isn’t listening.
She’s running to lower the cost of living, fix our health care system, and keep our promises to veterans and farmers. That’s the kind of work people need Congress to do. And Rachel has the experience to get to work on day one.
But with less than five weeks until Election Day, she needs more than our endorsement. She needs the resources to get her message in front of voters and make her case through the finish line.
Republican super PACs and MAGA megadonors are pouring money into these races. When our fundraising numbers go public, they’ll be looking to see whether we can keep up the fight. I want them to see a team that’s ready to see this through.
**Small Town PAC needs to raise $60,000 before midnight to help candidates like Rachel compete and win. Every contribution before tonight’s deadline helps us show that strength and fund the work ahead.**
**[Peter, will you split $5 or whatever works for you between Rachel Wallace and Small Town PAC before midnight? Let’s help Rachel flip this seat, take back the House, and give our communities the representation they deserve.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260930-rw.zJJafi&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-1159&t=2&akid=1159%2E34582%2EuSJY0s)**

Tim Walz

I know how exhausting it is to open your phone every day to another round of bad news. Prices keep rising, our healthcare system is worsening, and we’re being dragged through another endless war. _But we cannot afford to tune out and give up._ That’s exactly what they’re counting on. I don’t believe we’re defined by what we do when things are easy. We’re defined by how we stand together when the pressure is on. I don’t have to tell Minnesotans about that — our state knows in our bones what it means to step up. Resiliency is built into who we are. We’ve stood shoulder-to-shoulder time and again to reject this administration’s dangerous overreach and to protect our neighbors. Now, that same resolve has to power our fight through to November, because what we do in the next few weeks will shape the next few years. We can let this administration continue abusing their unchecked power — or we can hold them accountable and focus on building a government that works for _every_ Minnesotan and American. **Our last quarterly fundraising deadline of the election is tonight at midnight, and I’m pushing hard to reach my team’s big $20,000 online fundraising goal before then. Will you chip in to my re-election campaign before midnight so I can hit this goal and keep fighting for our country in Congress?** You can use this secure link: **[_https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140307379/650205024/-1066768109?source=260930em_km_deadline&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkzOTAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZmM1NDc0M2MtZWFiYy1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Nps-SiBSWsblprSG_cVEvNMesN9bSVqxNVSUb_yG7KA=)** If you can’t afford to donate right now, I completely understand — I’m glad to have you on the team no matter what.Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. With gratitude and resolve,
Kelly

body:
| It’s Gwen Graham
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/14475?t=4&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm) Peter,

Let me introduce myself.

My name is Gwen Graham, and I’ve spent most of my life in service to Florida families in one form or another – in our schools, our communities, and even in Congress, representing North Florida.

That's where I met David Jolly, more than a decade ago. We worked together to get things done for Florida families. So when we tell you we can govern together, it's because we already have. **[_I’m proud to be David’s running mate, and now I’m reaching out to ask for your support. Can you make a donation of any amount – split between our campaign and Blue Amp Action – to help us finish the end of Quarter 3 strong?_](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16703?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Jolly-Graham_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=5&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm)** _If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to David Jolly and Blue Amp Action will go through immediately:_ | [DONATE $12 →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16704?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Jolly-Graham_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=6&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm)

---
My dad, Bob Graham, served as Florida’s Governor and Senator. Even when he was in office, he still spent full workdays alongside the people he served, paving roads, teaching classes, and bagging groceries. He’s the one who taught me that two things matter in a leader: competency and character. Can people trust what you say, and can they trust you'll work hard for them and be able to get things done for them? I've carried that lesson forward. I once spent a workday as a high school student, just to see what our kids walk into every morning.

That's my approach to public service, and that’s the kind of leadership I want back in Tallahassee. Leaders who show up, listen, and remember who they work for.
**[_Peter, time is running out to raise the money our campaign will need to elect David Jolly and bring a new era of leadership to Florida – leadership that will support working families and change the future for our children. Will you contribute before midnight with a split donation between this campaign and Blue Amp Action?_](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16703?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Jolly-Graham_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=10&akid=3283%2E259176%2E9mhzmm)**

Gwen Graham

name: Ted Cruz
subject: You’re carrying the Party on your back
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
Nowhere else to turn...
Nowhere else to turn...

| | | | _**_A Personal Note from Senator Ted Cruz_**_
---
| | | Fellow American, Please allow me to be frank. **_We are on the brink of MISSING our fundraising goal for the FINAL FEC-mandated end-of-quarter deadline._****_ _** But this problem runs much deeper than not having enough money in the bank. It points to the same problem I've called attention to since last year... _Ever since we took back the White House and the Senate, Democrat voters have been energized and mobilizing while Republican voters have been sitting on the sidelines_. _We 're seeing it in elections, we're seeing it on the ground, we're seeing it in our voter verification numbers, and we're certainly seeing it in our fundraising.__ _ So, how are we still standing despite all of these negative metrics?_ _ **Our Party 's enthusiasm is being carried on the backs of just a select few conservatives... and that's _YOU_.**_ _ The fact that you're even reading this email right now proves it. _And so I hope you can understand why I 've decided to turn to YOU out of millions at this final hour_. _(I understand that things are still tough as we recover from four years of Biden 's inflationary disaster. | | Dear Peter,
Tonight at 11:59 PM, our campaign hits its FEC quarterly fundraising deadline, and in just 5 days, voters across Ohio's 8th District begin casting their ballots.
This is the moment that counts.
The number we report tonight will be public. Reporters, donors, and national partners will read it to decide whether this race is competitive. A strong finish tells them what we already know: with the new district lines, this seat is within reach, and we are running to win it.
We can't afford to take our foot off the gas now. Every dollar we raise before midnight goes straight into reaching voters during early voting: door knocks, phone calls, texts, and mail that remind families we're fighting to lower their costs, protect their electric bills from data center price hikes, and make government work for them again.
Will you chip in before midnight to help us close out this quarter strong?****

Hey folks,
Barack Obama is heading back onto the campaign trail with the midterms just a month away, and we're breaking down what his return means for Democratic candidates across the country.
We get into Obama's upcoming Senate fundraising, his appearances with candidates in Iowa and Texas, Trump's response to Obama's comments about women in government, and what the latest polling discussed in the episode says about the fight for the Senate.
* [**00:01:18**] Obama steps back into the midterm fight, with a Senate fundraising event scheduled for October 7 and more campaign appearances expected.
* [**00:02:29**] We look at Obama's role boosting Josh Turek in Iowa, and why his involvement with Democratic candidates could matter down the stretch.
* [**00:03:40**] Obama hits the taco shop with James Talarico in Texas as we talk about the contrast the episode draws between Democrats campaigning with Obama and Republicans' relationship with Trump.
* [**00:05:34**] Obama says he believes governments would be better with more women in charge, and Trump gets asked directly about those comments.
* [**00:08:10**] We turn to the Senate map, some extremely optimistic polling being discussed online, the uncertainty that comes with those numbers, and why Democrats still have a lot of work ahead of them.

There's real optimism in this episode, but there's also a warning: polls are snapshots, elections aren't won on social media, and no former president is coming back to save anybody. The bigger question is whether Democrats can turn this moment into lasting trust by showing people that government can actually improve their lives. That work matters long after November. clean_body: | = I know that this time of the month means you are receiving a heavy volume of fundraising emails. Believe me, they fill my inbox too. What bothers me about those messages is how often they manufacture a false sense of doom and gloom just to open your wallet. When I founded the Jane Fonda Climate PAC, I made a promise to do things differently. While there are deeply urgent crises in front of us — stopping authoritarianism, saving our planet, and ending Big Oil’s stranglehold on our politics — we refuse to fabricate a crisis just to ask for your support. I believe in being honest about the odds. = | = | = ---|--- The threats we face are very real: the deep pockets of fossil fuel corporations, corporate super PACs, and shady outside spenders are encroaching into every corner of our government. They are pouring millions of dollars into the races our candidates are competing in to seize control of city councils, state legislatures, utility boards, and Congress — the exact places where key decisions about your health, energy bills, and community are made. We’ve endorsed more candidates this year than ever before — over 200 fearless leaders. And with a little over a month left until Election Day, every single action we take right now will determine what happens at the ballot box. = = | = ---|--- Thank you so much for your continued support. In solidarity, Jane Fonda | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Peter,

In his desperate attempt to hold onto his House seat, Rep. Jimmy Gomez is
using his official office budget — money meant for serving constituents —
to pay for re-election campaign ads.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260930-1-agt.LugRjK&refcode=em20260930-38309&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38309%2E1203867%2Ef9DQ-4 ]Post on X from @city_of_sortz: "Jimmy Gomez is flooding mailboxes with
campaign ads PAID BY his Office Funds (resources meant to serve
constituents - not for campaigning) Vote for @Angela4CA for CA-34";
attached is an image of one of the mailers

priorities: he puts his personal interests and political career over the
people of Los Angeles.

His Justice Democrats-endorsed challenger, Angela Gonzales-Torres, said it
best:

“100 better uses for official funds come to mind, starting with air
monitors and conditioners in schools across CA-34. Grants for small
businesses. One in-person town hall. He chose mailers.”

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260930-1-agt.LugRjK&refcode=em20260930-38309&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=38309%2E1203867%2Ef9DQ-4 ]Help us elect Angela in less than 5 weeks: split a grassroots
contribution now!

working-class champion for her community. While she’s fighting for
affordable housing, clean air, abolishing ICE, ending the genocide in
Gaza, and passing Medicare for All, Jimmy is taking checks from AIPAC, the
real estate industry, Crypto and AI lobby groups, and corporate PACs
fueling the very crises we face.

She took Jimmy on in the Democratic primary last June and secured a
top-two finish to advance to this November’s general election.

If we rally behind her, she can win the votes to unseat this Do-Nothing
Democrat in less than five weeks. But she faces her FINAL end-of-quarter

I am furious that our cost of living, our jobs, our environment, our democracy, and our bodily autonomy are up for debate for as long as Republicans are in charge.
That's why I would dearly love to see them lose their jobs.
**We have an election coming, and with it, the opportunity of a lifetime. Let's not waste it.**
Across the country, Democratic pro-choice women have stepped up to take on Republicans and fight for something better. They're shouldering the attacks that come with challenging billionaires and megadonors who are used to getting their way.
We need to help those women finish the job.
They need resources to reach voters, answer those attacks, and keep fighting through the very last day. In a close race, just one more conversation, one more voter reached, or one more person getting to the polls can make all the difference.
That is why I'm asking for your donation today. There is still time to help Democratic women win, but every day we have left is precious.
We want win margins so decisive that the women we help elect will have a clear mandate to lead our country in a new direction and undo the disaster of the Trump years.
I want to help make that happen.

clean_body: | = Hi Peter, it's Ellen — founder of EMILYs List. I want Donald Trump to have a very bad election night this year. I want to watch Democratic pro-choice women beat Republicans everywhere. I want to see the U.S. House change hands, and Mike Johnson give up the gavel once and for all. I want to take back power in the Senate so our women can stop the MAGA agenda in its tracks. I want to hear victory speeches from women who are ready to walk into Congress and state legislatures and fight like hell for our rights. And I want you to be able to look at those results and say: I was part of that. We have just over five weeks to make this a reality. And with our 3X Match Fund ending tonight at midnight, this is your last chance before Election Day to make your donation go three times further for EMILYs List women. = | = I am furious that our cost of living, our jobs, our environment, our democracy, and our bodily autonomy are up for debate for as long as Republicans are in charge. That's why I would dearly love to see them lose their jobs. We have an election coming, and with it, the opportunity of a lifetime. Let's not waste it. Across the country, Democratic pro-choice women have stepped up to take on Republicans and fight for something better. They're shouldering the attacks that come with challenging billionaires and megadonors who are used to getting their way. We need to help those women finish the job. They need resources to reach voters, answer those attacks, and keep fighting through the very last day. In a close race, just one more conversation, one more voter reached, or one more person getting to the polls can make all the difference. That is why I'm asking for your donation today. There is still time to help Democratic women win, but every day we have left is precious. We want win margins so decisive that the women we help elect will have a clear mandate to lead our country in a new direction and undo the disaster of the Trump years. So even as we call out Donald Trump for orchestrating attacks on our democracy, we also need to highlight his state-level allies (read: enthusiastic enablers) who put his plots into motion. **Sometimes that means we zoom in on one state at a time. In this email, we’re... choosing Texas. Let’s take a look at a few of Trump’s favorite puppets in the Lone Star State[and how this team can prevent anti-democracy extremists from doing more damage.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140312425/650221326/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_VillainsofDemocracy_email_20260930-NDRC-Tier1-VillainsofDemocracy_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260930-NDRC-Tier1-VillainsofDemocracy_&utm_campaign=VillainsofDemocracy&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNhYzBjMWM5LWYxYmMtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ywHsZ0X3NQPXxbg8Kblv7yMNneu2OinkVvvr6BLJz1w=)** This year’s elections in Texas aren’t just a chance to hold map manipulators accountable — they’re an opportunity to stop the next power grab before it starts. **Governor Greg Abbott:** He kicked off the national redistricting crisis last year by calling a special session and pushing a mid-decade gerrymander — targeting five Democratic-held districts and reducing the voting power of communities of color. **_How we can prevent him from doing more damage:_ We can DEFEAT him this November.** We’ve endorsed Democracy Defender Gina Hinojosa, who’s giving Abbott the fiercest challenge ever since he took the governor’s seat. If she wins, it wouldn’t just send a strong message to other GOP governors hoping to manipulate their maps — but Hinojosa would be in a position to veto future gerrymanders that Texas Republican lawmakers are expected to try to pass. [**Rush a donation now to help power Democracy Defenders to victory across the country and grow our movement for fair maps and fair elections.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140312426/650221327/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_VillainsofDemocracy_email_20260930-NDRC-Tier1-VillainsofDemocracy_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260930-NDRC-Tier1-VillainsofDemocracy_&utm_campaign=VillainsofDemocracy&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNhYzBjMWM5LWYxYmMtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ywHsZ0X3NQPXxbg8Kblv7yMNneu2OinkVvvr6BLJz1w=) **Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows and Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick: **They’re the leaders who drove the new gerrymander forward in the Texas House and Senate. Patrick had the gall to justify it by saying, "We’re a red state, we deserve more representation." Deserve! So much for the Texans who deserve fair representation. _**How we can prevent them from doing more damage:**_ We’ve endorsed more than 70 Democracy Defenders for the Texas House who will stand up for fair maps and fair elections. Republicans currently hold a majority in that chamber, but we can narrow their margin, invest in the long-term fight to take back control, and make it that much harder for the GOP to redraw Texas again before 2028. [**Every day, supporters like you help make it possible to elect leaders who fight extreme gerrymanders and preserve the integrity of our elections. So even as we call out Donald Trump for orchestrating attacks on our democracy, we also need to highlight his state-level allies (read: enthusiastic enablers) who put his plots into motion. Governor Greg Abbott: He kicked off the national redistricting crisis last year by calling a special session and pushing a mid-decade gerrymander — targeting five Democratic-held districts and reducing the voting power of communities of color. How we can prevent him from doing more damage: We can DEFEAT him this November. We’ve endorsed Democracy Defender Gina Hinojosa, who’s giving Abbott the fiercest challenge ever since he took the governor’s seat. Patrick had the gall to justify it by saying, "We’re a red state, we deserve more representation." Deserve! So much for the Texans who deserve fair representation. How we can prevent them from doing more damage: We’ve endorsed more than 70 Democracy Defenders for the Texas House who will stand up for fair maps and fair elections. name: Mary Peltola
subject: New polling from Alaska
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
Hello. It’s Mary.

I’m writing to you to ask if you can make a donation to help me win the
Senate seat in Alaska. A new poll shows me WINNING this race in round two
of Alaska’s ranked choice voting system – so your support will help build
momentum in these final weeks and turn this poll into reality.

If you know how critical this election is for Alaska and the whole country
– and you are fired up to take action – then please use this link to split
a donation between my campaign for Senate and Demand Justice PAC:

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260930-2-split-mp.nYGNhP&refcode=em20260930-61865&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=61865%2E1407376%2EiwNRyk ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dj-em-20260930-2-split-mp

The fight for fish, family, freedom is clearly a fight worth having. See
for yourself:

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260930-2-split-mp.nYGNhP&refcode=em20260930-61865&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=61865%2E1407376%2EiwNRyk ]Tweet by Alaska Survey Research: LATEST: Mary Peltola continues to lead
incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan in pivotal Alaska Senate contest. Alaska
Survey Research, September 10-12, 2026, N=1,352 likely Alaska voters,
MOE=+/-3.0%. Peltola hits 50% in Round 2 against her three opponents.

But we can’t look at a
good poll and become complacent. In fact, this is a sign that we need to
scale up now because polls don’t win elections.

Plus, Dan Sullivan and his dark money backers see these polls, and they
realize that we have what it takes to flip this Senate seat. So they’re
spending big to stop us, flooding Alaska with ads, mailers, and more to
try and slow us down.

To fight back, we need to ace this final FEC end-of-quarter deadline next
week to show everyone watching that we can turn these polls into power.

That’s why we need a huge number of donations today. I’m counting on those
of you who understand the importance of this race and last EOQ deadline to
make a donation today before it’s too late. So I’m personally asking:

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260930-2-split-mp.nYGNhP&refcode=em20260930-61865&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61865%2E1407376%2EiwNRyk ]Will you split a donation between my campaign for U.S. Senate in Alaska
and Demand Justice PAC before tonight's deadline? No matter how much you
can afford to chip in today, it all adds up when lots of us are chipping
in.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260930-2-split-mp.nYGNhP&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-61865&t=1022&akid=61865%2E1407376%2EiwNRyk ]Donate $5 ››

As long as we all work together, we will win Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat.

The strength of this campaign has always come from regular people stepping
up when it counted. And it means a lot to me that so many of you have
faith in our ability to win. Together, we’re building a movement.

Thanks for being a part of it.

- Mary

683 registered Democrats were asked a simple question:

* 87% of Democrats would feel positive if President Trump were impeached.
* 83% of Democrats would feel excited or indifferent if Trump died in his sleep.
* 57% of Democrats would feel excited or indifferent if Trump were assassinated.

**[This isn't fringe. Commerce posted a final **[2.2% annualized second-quarter GDP reading](https://substack.com/redirect/95178aee-e5c8-4839-ac38-c0e254df0e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/95178aee-e5c8-4839-ac38-c0e254df0e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Wednesday, above the 1.5% forecast, while August outlays rose 0.9% and yearly **[inflation held at 3.4%.](https://substack.com/redirect/0c0ef74b-6977-4fe0-8cce-f030984df22c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/03d06cfb-45b1-4f30-8fcb-6c344a202159?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revision beat prior print:** The last Q2 estimate is 2.2%, up from the 1.5% figure Commerce had on the books, with households and businesses both spending more than the earlier report showed.
* **Private demand ran hotter:** Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, Commerce's gauge of underlying demand, was marked up to 4.6% for April through June.
* **August shoppers kept spending:** Household spending rose 0.9%. The department tied part of that jump to pricier fuel at retail pumps. Personal income slowed to a 0.2% gain from 0.3%.
* **Inflation held firm anyway:** Separate August data left the 12-month rate at 3.4%, matching July. Prices rose 0.3% on the month and core PCE rose 0.2%, both quicker than July.

After a White House meeting with technology chiefs on Tuesday, President Donald Trump signed an order telling federal agencies to drop the label "artificial intelligence" and **[switch to"Super Intelligence."](https://substack.com/redirect/9b9f8b47-fa84-4ad5-9be7-66b2ae6e2aef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Agencies drop old terms:** Letters, websites, reports, and other non-statute materials must use "Super Intelligence" or "SI." The White House said agencies should "no longer acknowledge" "artificial intelligence" and "AI."
* **Definition work comes next:** The president's science and technology assistant is told to write a federal definition of SI and propose extra executive steps to put the new vocabulary in force.
* **Accord called morally binding:** Trump said the executives signed a White House Accord on Super Intelligence that is "morally binding," and that they "almost viewed it as a separate kind of constitution."
* **Johnson frames voluntary accord:** Speaker Mike Johnson called it a voluntary statement of principles. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote that "every major American lab" pledged "robust internal controls and multiple layers of audits and reviews."

# [Hiring rebounded to 90k after a three-month lull](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
ADP counted **[90,000 new private jobs in September,](https://substack.com/redirect/d20f7ca7-46cb-4002-b135-01ed86a10f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** above the 68,000 Dow Jones and WSJ forecasts and up from a revised 36,000 in August, a day ahead of Friday's Labor Department report.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Health services led hiring:** Education and health services supplied 55,000 of the new jobs. Leisure and hospitality added 22,000, factories 17,000 and builders 15,000.
* **Pay growth stayed solid:** Year-over-year base wages were up 3.2% and total pay ran 4.7% higher. Chief economist Nela Richardson called it "a strong report" after hiring had cooled for 3 months.
* **Finance payrolls turned negative:** Finance lost 16,000 jobs, professional and business services lost 11,000, and mining plus natural resources lost 1,000.
* **Services outpaced goods producers:** Service firms created 59,000 jobs and goods producers 31,000. The Northeast added 56,000, and companies with 50 to 499 employees added 54,000.

# [Boeing now owns the Air Force AND Navy sixth-gen fighter contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Boeing **[stock rose 2% Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/786655bf-78f1-4da8-8501-b511d755d80e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the Defense Department chose it, **[not Northrop Grumman,](https://substack.com/redirect/06e0065f-cd9a-4e4c-b8ea-6b4f2fa7e26b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to build the Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX Strike Fighter.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Development award tops $20B:** Pentagon figures put the full-scale development phase above $20 billion, giving Boeing the Navy carrier-fighter program.
* **Air Force win booked:** The company already won the Air Force's parallel jet, the F-47, in March 2025, so it now holds both U.S. sixth-generation fighter lines.
* **Street saw Boeing favored:** BNP Paribas analyst Matthew Akers said investors treated Boeing as the likely Navy pick even after the F-47 award.
* **St. Louis capacity expands:** Boeing is pouring new manufacturing space into St. Louis for the F-47 and says that site can support more than one next-generation aircraft program.

# [7.30% mortgages just pushed applications down 6%](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Last week's 30-year conforming rate **[reached 7.30%, the sixth weekly increase,](https://substack.com/redirect/9fe5a8d6-0616-4608-a79d-921cc1c095c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as MBA **[applications slid 6%](https://substack.com/redirect/ad1506cb-a1ba-447c-afca-860b9a0fcd33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to a two-year low and Realtor.com counted price cuts on a record 20.8% of September listings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Conforming rate keeps climbing:** Mortgages capped at $832,750 moved to 7.30% from 7.12%. Points, including origination on 20% down, sat at 0.75. Mortgage News Daily printed 7.58% Tuesday, the most since November 2023.
* **Applications hit two-year low:** Refinance filings fell 9% week to week and 56% from a year earlier. Purchase filings were down 4% on the week and 14% from last year, MBA economist Joel Kan said.
* **Sellers cut prices anyway:** Realtor.com put September reductions on 20.8% of active listings, a September record, as listings rose 5.4% to more than 1.161 million homes.
* **Pending sales still sliding:** Contracts were 4.1% below a year ago. Jake Krimmel said the 30-year has jumped almost 40 basis points in 4 weeks and more than 1 point since the Iran war started in late February.

# [Europe spent €100B extra for the same oil and gas](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
EU capitals[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/46f71eb3-9eb0-4ccd-806d-af7ea3ebb208?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[are stacking price caps, tax cuts, and aid](https://substack.com/redirect/46f71eb3-9eb0-4ccd-806d-af7ea3ebb208?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while Brent lingers near $100 a barrel. JPMorgan told clients it no longer has a baseline for how the Iran-linked disruption ends.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bank drops its baseline:** In a Sept. 17 note the bank said, "We simply don't know how to model the endgame," after oil above $100 failed to force talks. It said $90 would have matched known supply and demand.
* **Global inventories keep draining:** The IEA's September report recorded a further 95 million-barrel drop in August. Combined losses since February reach 507 million barrels, roughly 2.8 million barrels a day.
* **Germany leads next wave:** From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31 Berlin will shave energy tax 14 cents a liter, about 17 cents after VAT, inside a €2.5 billion package. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said daily drivers "are reaching their breaking point."
* **Subsidy club keeps growing:** IEA tallies show fuel-subsidy countries rising from 16 to 38 and energy-tax cuts from 40 to 57. Pew, using mid-June IEA counts, found 113 countries with at least one post-war energy-cost step.

# [Tariffs unlocked a $15B steel mill and 1,750 Iowa jobs](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
AISI CEO Kevin Dempsey said the $15 billion Iowa mill Trump announced with Mesabi Metallics **[shows tariff walls are giving firms the nerve](https://substack.com/redirect/4e2c0d23-d416-4096-a9bc-a1c2f9700896?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to fund new U.S. plants with their own cash.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Largest U.S. mill planned:** Output is slated to reach 10 million tons a year from Mesabi's new Minnesota ore mine, about 2 million tons more than the prior U.S. record mill.
* **America ranks third globally:** Dempsey said the United States overtook Japan last year for third place behind China and India, yet still supplies only 4% of world steel.
* **Imports already dropped sharply:** He credited tariffs with cutting inbound steel from 44 million tons in 2014 to 25 million tons last year and said Canada should copy that shield.
* **Private capital follows tariffs:** First-term steel policy, he said, restored confidence so companies will put private money into mills instead of watching foreign surplus wreck the bet.

# [Disney just cut hundreds of HR and technology jobs](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Walt Disney is[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/89c646ea-6deb-41c5-965d-cae6a61e0f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[cutting a few hundred human-resources and technology jobs,](https://substack.com/redirect/89c646ea-6deb-41c5-965d-cae6a61e0f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Reuters said, another round under CEO Josh D'Amaro as the company adjusts to AI tools and streaming rivals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/763ae860-82eb-47e2-9019-26caf9744afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Latest cuts hit support:** The new wave lands in HR and technology. In April the company already removed about 1,000 roles from marketing, studio and television, ESPN, products, technology and corporate staff.
* **July hit creative units:** A July round removed several hundred more people at Pixar, ESPN, the film studio and Disney Entertainment Television.
* **Early retirement window opened:** August packages were limited to directors through executive vice presidents in Entertainment, ESPN and corporate who were 50 or older with at least 10 years at the company.
* **Workforce still large:** Fiscal 2025 ended with about 231,000 workers, including about 172,000 in the United States. Iger-era 2023 cuts took out 7,000 jobs in a $5.5 billion savings drive.

JPMorgan told clients it no longer has a baseline for how the Iran-linked disruption ends. | | ---|---|--- Bank drops its baseline: In a Sept. 17 note the bank said, "We simply don't know how to model the endgame," after oil above $100 failed to force talks. It said $90 would have matched known supply and demand. Global inventories keep draining: The IEA's September report recorded a further 95 million-barrel drop in August. Combined losses since February reach 507 million barrels, roughly 2.8 million barrels a day. Germany leads next wave: From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31 Berlin will shave energy tax 14 cents a liter, about 17 cents after VAT, inside a €2.5 billion package. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said daily drivers "are reaching their breaking point." Subsidy club keeps growing: IEA tallies show fuel-subsidy countries rising from 16 to 38 and energy-tax cuts from 40 to 57. Pew, using mid-June IEA counts, found 113 countries with at least one post-war energy-cost step. AISI CEO Kevin Dempsey said the $15 billion Iowa mill Trump announced with Mesabi Metallics to fund new U.S. plants with their own cash. | | ---|---|--- Largest U.S. mill planned: Output is slated to reach 10 million tons a year from Mesabi's new Minnesota ore mine, about 2 million tons more than the prior U.S. record mill. America ranks third globally: Dempsey said the United States overtook Japan last year for third place behind China and India, yet still supplies only 4% of world steel. Imports already dropped sharply: He credited tariffs with cutting inbound steel from 44 million tons in 2014 to 25 million tons last year and said Canada should copy that shield. Private capital follows tariffs: First-term steel policy, he said, restored confidence so companies will put private money into mills instead of watching foreign surplus wreck the bet. Walt Disney is Reuters said, another round under CEO Josh D'Amaro as the company adjusts to AI tools and streaming rivals. | | ---|---|--- Latest cuts hit support: The new wave lands in HR and technology. In April the company already removed about 1,000 roles from marketing, studio and television, ESPN, products, technology and corporate staff. July hit creative units: A July round removed several hundred more people at Pixar, ESPN, the film studio and Disney Entertainment Television. Early retirement window opened: August packages were limited to directors through executive vice presidents in Entertainment, ESPN and corporate who were 50 or older with at least 10 years at the company. Workforce still large: Fiscal 2025 ended with about 231,000 workers, including about 172,000 in the United States. Iger-era 2023 cuts took out 7,000 jobs in a $5.5 billion savings drive. name: Gavin Newsom
subject: Deb Haaland
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
Friend: it’s Governor Gavin Newsom.

With 34 days until Election Day and 6 days until voting begins in New Mexico, this is a message for you:

Groceries and gas prices are up. Wages aren’t keeping pace. Families are getting squeezed. People are fed up and Donald Trump isn't slowing down. He's attacking immigrant communities, threatening healthcare, rolling back voting rights, and testing the limits of his power every day.

_This November, New Mexico has the power to fight back by electing Deb Haaland as Governor.
_
**_[That's why I'm asking you to chip in to Deb Haaland's campaign today. Will you rush $5 to help Deb reach her $250,000 final end-of-quarter goal so she has the resources to keep New Mexico blue and defend working families from Trump's attacks?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16412?refcode=jtk1448-fr-nd&t=1&akid=12847%2E400544%2EQyBoJq)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16411?refcode=jtk1448-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12847%2E400544%2EQyBoJq)
---
Friend, here’s the truth: Donald Trump and his MAGA allies don’t want you to elect Deb Haaland as New Mexico’s next Governor. **_Here’s why:_**
Deb has spent her career fighting back when New Mexicans are under attack and delivering results when it matters most. So those Medicaid, SNAP, and WIC cuts that Republicans are pushing? Deb has a record of protecting healthcare when Trump was President. Those public lands under attack from Donald Trump? Deb has spent her career protecting them from irresponsible oil and gas drilling and standing as a brick wall against the very cuts Trump has tried to make. When Republicans undermine our elections and try to make it harder to vote for their unpopular extremist agenda, Deb has been one of the strongest advocates fighting to protect voting rights and make sure everyone has a voice. That's what got her started as a leader when she knocked thousands of doors in Indian Country to make sure Native voices were heard.
Deb Haaland has the experience and the fight to deliver lower costs, protect rural healthcare from devastating cuts, and protect New Mexicans from Donald Trump's extremist agenda. New Mexico has been a leader in so many ways, from providing Universal Childcare to supplementing SNAP benefits when Donald Trump politicized hunger and barring armed federal agents from polling places. **_All of that is on the line._**

Now, the question is whether Deb has the grassroots support to win in 34 days. That means she needs you, friend. _[Can I please count on you to contribute $5, or whatever you can afford, to Deb Haaland's campaign to help close the gap on her final end-of-quarter goal? Even a few dollars will help elect a Governor who's ready for this fight.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16412?refcode=jtk1448-fr-nd&t=3&akid=12847%2E400544%2EQyBoJq)_
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $10](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16425?refcode=jtk1448-fr-nd&t=4&akid=12847%2E400544%2EQyBoJq)
---

---

---
| | [Other Amount](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16411?refcode=jtk1448-fr-nd&t=7&akid=12847%2E400544%2EQyBoJq)
---
The next few years will be defined by who shows up. Thank you for showing up today.

Gavin Newsom

Fellow Patriot,

My opponent, Annie Andrews, is spending millions of dollars, hoping that South Carolina will forget her radical views.

She called the Save Women's Sports Act _**“shameful.”**_
She doesn't support the Second Amendment. _**She's a paid gun-control advocate.**_

**She's too radical for South Carolina.**

Friends,
Today is the last day of the quarter, which in the world of campaigns and elections means one thing: **This is the last test of strength before early voting starts** _._ That's right. The FEC end-of-quarter deadline I've been talking about in some of my recent posts is at midnight tonight.
After tonight, campaigns across the country will be working on submitting one of the final fundraising reports of the cycle. Once those numbers are public, everyone -- _and I do mean everyone_ -- will be checking to see who's got the resources to be competitive and who's fallen short.
In terms of important moments in the campaign, this one is monumental. In fact, it might be one of the most critical in these final days -- and right now, I'm worried because, despite the amazing grassroots support we've received, we're starting to slow down.
In a moment, I'm going to ask you to **[chip in and help us close the gap](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a06b75a-dcac-4fd7-a5ae-acb612c0d670?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. But first, let me back up for a second and explain why that matters.
My team and I set an ambitious end-of-quarter goal to raise $1 million. We did that because, after seeing our campaign's incredible surge of momentum, my opponent Roger Marshall and his allies have spent millions in an attempt to crush our movement and destroy our 2-point lead. Now, with just weeks left in this race, we _must_ hit our goal to have any hope of fighting back.
**If we** close the gap __(and with the help of supporters like you, I _know_ we can), it will send a powerful message that our momentum isn't a fluke. It will show everyone we have what it takes to hold on to our lead, defeat Roger Marshall and fight back against the corrupt and chaotic policies coming out of Washington.
**But if we** miss our goal, that will send a powerful message too, but it will be the wrong one. If we fall short, Marshall and the super PACs backing him will think we're vulnerable. If that happens, they'll almost certainly increase their spending and their attacks in these crucial final weeks before Election Day, and we won't have the budget to respond.
**After multiple election forecasters shifted this race in our favor yet again, Marshall and his allies know Kansas is a true battleground. They 're watching for **_**any**_**sign that we don 't have what it takes to go the distance.**
The only way to show them we do is to hit this goal. That's how we send the message, loud and clear, that Kansans and the country are fed up with their disastrous policies. Fed up with prices skyrocketing while healthcare and food assistance programs are cut. Fed up with leaders who turn their backs on the people they're supposed to represent.
Hitting our target shows them people are ready for something better. It helps us make sure every single voter hears our unifying message, proves to everyone watching that we'll stand up to chaos and corruption and shows the nation the power of our movement.
**[With the deadline just hours away, time really is running out, though. That's why I have to ask: If you can, will you chip in whatever you can spare to help us across the finish line?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a06b75a-dcac-4fd7-a5ae-acb612c0d670?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Every dollar truly does make a difference when thousands of people pitch in, so please, chip in anything you can and help me send the message to Marshall and everyone watching that we've got what it takes to win this thing.
[DONATE](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a06b75a-dcac-4fd7-a5ae-acb612c0d670?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for your support,
Adam Hamilton

Our volunteers helped them register, fix their registration, or make a plan to vote, and we'll stay with them until their ballot is cast.

name: Jeff Bridges
subject: 64 counties. No copy-and-paste solutions.
body:
There’s really no substitute for standing on someone's front porch and hearing what’s on their mind. You learn things you simply can't from polls.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/996bfb2040e7/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379145?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/MTufYmCCCyE?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Sunday started with breakfast at Fitch Ranch Cafe in Granby, then coffee at Simple Coffee in Fraser. Excellent food and coffee, go if you get the chance.
I joined Phil Weiser, Joe Neguse, and a room full of volunteers ready to knock doors for Liz Newsom, Democratic candidate for Clerk and Recorder. Then headed out to the doors.
**There’s really no substitute for standing on someone's front porch and hearing what’s on their mind. You learn things you simply can't learn from polls. You get the texture behind our cost-of-living crisis.**
---
|
---
| | In Fraser, that means hearing how a world-class ski resort just down the road creates jobs and opportunity, while also pushing housing further out of reach for the folks who live and work there. And how local governments can help—or hurt.
After a morning of conversations in Grand County, we hopped back in the car and headed to Clear Creek County for a rally on Main Street with local Democrats.
---
|
---
| | **What Fraser and Idaho Springs have in common with every other place I've visited across our state is a cost-of-living crisis. But we can't solve it with one answer copied and pasted into all 64 counties. The headline may be the same. The particulars aren't.**
---
|
---
| | That’s one of my favorite parts of running statewide. You start to see that the problem may be shared, but the devil and the divine are in the details.
Understanding what's actually happening requires showing up, knocking doors, and listening. More towns. More doors. More conversations.
More miles ahead.

---
| | Talk soon,
ps If you haven’t had the chance to go leaf peeping yet, make plans to do so this weekend. The colors were already peak Colorado!
---

# WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 2026
---
**A Note from Cole, CEO of The Flyover** **Dear Reader,** Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations--on the books for decades, published for anyone to read--is a remarkable sentence. It says the word terrorist "can be a barrier rather than an aid to understanding." The written policy is that the plainest true word for an act of terror gets in the way of understanding it. That's not one outlet's quirk. It's mainstream media doctrine. And last month, you got to see where doctrine like that leads. Ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, reporters at another major news organization, a national public broadcaster, received a memo from the standards office: "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks." The approved language for the deadliest terrorist attack in American history, in which nearly 3,000 people were murdered, was "hijackings that led to plane crashes." The memo leaked. Two days later, the broadcaster backed down. Sort of. They carved out an exception for 9/11, and only 9/11. The rule stands. And their defense was telling. They didn't argue that the rule is right. They argued that it's the industry standard and that newsrooms everywhere follow the same practice. The worst part is, they're right. It is the standard. That's the problem. You know why we exist. The truth isn't a barrier to understanding. It's the only road there. The facts arrive the way we found them, in plain words, and you decide what they mean. That's your job, and we'd never dream of doing it for you. We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. A terrorist attack is a terrorist attack. We'd print that sentence any day of the week. No memo required. So today I'm asking: if news that calls things what they are is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind it? Support the news in plain words. Free, every morning. clean_body: Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations... | | | | | WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 A Note from Cole, CEO of The Flyover Dear Reader, Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations--on the books for decades, published for anyone to read--is a remarkable sentence. It says the word terrorist "can be a barrier rather than an aid to understanding." The written policy is that the plainest true word for an act of terror gets in the way of understanding it. That's not one outlet's quirk. It's mainstream media doctrine. And last month, you got to see where doctrine like that leads. Ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, reporters at another major news organization, a national public broadcaster, received a memo from the standards office: "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks." The approved language for the deadliest terrorist attack in American history, in which nearly 3,000 people were murdered, was "hijackings that led to plane crashes." The memo leaked. Two days later, the broadcaster backed down. Sort of. They carved out an exception for 9/11, and only 9/11. The rule stands. And their defense was telling. They didn't argue that the rule is right. They argued that it's the industry standard and that newsrooms everywhere follow the same practice. The worst part is, they're right. It is the standard. That's the problem. You know why we exist. The truth isn't a barrier to understanding. It's the only road there. The facts arrive the way we found them, in plain words, and you decide what they mean. That's your job, and we'd never dream of doing it for you. We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And The Flyover stays free. A terrorist attack is a terrorist attack. We'd print that sentence any day of the week. No memo required. So today I'm asking: if news that calls things what they are is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind it? Support the news in plain words. Free, every morning. Make a generous donation to support The Flyover. Our promise: we answer to you. Help us keep it. -- Cole CEO, The Flyover | | The Flyover, LLC 1910 Thomes Ave. Cheyenne WY 82001 | ---|---

Auto insurance rates are influenced by many factors, including repair costs, vehicle values, claims trends, location, and broader market conditions. And because every insurer evaluates these factors differently, the price offered for similar coverage can vary from one company to another. That's where [Insurify](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskL1uwyAUhZ8Gb4ngQvgZGCpF2dK1o0XgOkbCxoLb_Lx95U59gG6fdM75hvN1Ha8hl7zeP8OCnl5THROmHANhGld89oJE2Mbn_A4Ne13C-k4tP7D1_p0SriNw0AfuDpL_WYoh-RtPTgzohXHcOKGVG2bvUKsoOJyileEUFQqwdoKILgadAIbsdyF3kgvLDZij0gYmjPFmknThFpnimDLVdqQZCV-hT-VdH9iOsS5D8TPR1pn8YHBhcNlaJYyEqW6U69r30p7IS2DyLJQ9MdBxR2th5y6YPA_Np-2ZS8ldG6b4fQm5_PrpPz96ePgJAAD__ywLf3Y) can help. Insurify is a comparison platform that lets you check auto insurance quotes from multiple insurers in one place, side-by-side, in just a few minutes. Instead of manually visiting multiple insurance websites, you answer a few questions once and can quickly see available options from different carriers. For families with multiple vehicles, teen drivers, long commutes, or an upcoming renewal, comparing available rates could uncover meaningful savings. Even a modest difference each month can add up over the course of a year. [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskL1uwyAUhZ8Gb4ngQvgZGCpF2dK1o0XgOkbCxoLb_Lx95U59gG6fdM75hvN1Ha8hl7zeP8OCnl5THROmHANhGld89oJE2Mbn_A4Ne13C-k4tP7D1_p0SriNw0AfuDpL_WYoh-RtPTgzohXHcOKGVG2bvUKsoOJyileEUFQqwdoKILgadAIbsdyF3kgvLDZij0gYmjPFmknThFpnimDLVdqQZCV-hT-VdH9iOsS5D8TPR1pn8YHBhcNlaJYyEqW6U69r30p7IS2DyLJQ9MdBxR2th5y6YPA_Np-2ZS8ldG6b4fQm5_PrpPz96ePgJAAD__ywLf3Y) The important thing to remember is that insurance rates aren't one-size-fits-all. clean_body: Your car insurance renews, you glance at the number, and the price has changed. ** | | | | | Wednesday, September 30, 2026 Dear Flyover Reader, Today's partner is , and honestly, this is one of those things that just makes sense to check. Car insurance rates have gone up a lot recently, and it only takes a few minutes to compare quotes and see if you could save money. The process is simple, and there's really no downside to seeing what other options are out there. -Cole, CEO A lot of people have had the same experience lately. Your car insurance renews, you glance at the number, and the price has changed. Maybe by $20 a month. Maybe by $50. Maybe more. Even when your car, driving habits, and record haven't changed, the price you pay for coverage can still fluctuate. Auto insurance rates are influenced by many factors, including repair costs, vehicle values, claims trends, location, and broader market conditions. And because every insurer evaluates these factors differently, the price offered for similar coverage can vary from one company to another. That's where can help. Insurify is a comparison platform that lets you check auto insurance quotes from multiple insurers in one place, side-by-side, in just a few minutes. Instead of manually visiting multiple insurance websites, you answer a few questions once and can quickly see available options from different carriers. For families with multiple vehicles, teen drivers, long commutes, or an upcoming renewal, comparing available rates could uncover meaningful savings. Even a modest difference each month can add up over the course of a year. The important thing to remember is that insurance rates aren't one-size-fits-all. Different carriers may offer different prices based on your individual circumstances, which means the company that offered a competitive rate in the past may not necessarily have the best available option for you today. That's why periodically comparing quotes can be worthwhile. name: Gina
subject: Thank you for opening this email.
body:
Hi Peter, it’s Gina. I wanted to
send a quick note before the end of the day to share my deepest gratitude.

Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for being in this fight with us. I
know how crowded your inbox gets, especially during the end of the month
and deadline days. Plenty of other politicians have sent you panicked
emails today even though they have millions sitting safely in the bank.

But that’s not what this is.

We’re facing massive spending from Greg Abbott and his billionaire allies
against us, and if we don’t raise enough funds, we face the very real
threat of having to go dark on the airwaves.

I genuinely mean that. This Texas sized campaign is powered by people like
you, and I’m grateful that it is. Because of you, this is officially the
closest Texas governor's race in a generation, but we seriously can’t
afford to lose momentum right now.

I know I can win this race; I feel it in my bones, but only if we have the
resources to stay on the air and on the doors through November 3rd.

My team set a goal of raising $2 million by tonight to keep our campaign
running, and whether we pull ahead of Abbott depends entirely on
grassroots supporters stepping up right now.

So I’m personally asking: will you make a donation today to power our

Peter,

| | | Tonight, at midnight, we are required to report our fundraising numbers for the last time before the election. Every dollar Equal Opportunity Now has raised this quarter gets filed with the FEC, and once it's filed, anyone can see it. Reporters covering the midterms. Political operatives sizing up who's real and who isn't. Republican strategists deciding which Democratic organizations are actually worth worrying about. Friends,**NEXT WEEK on Tuesday, October 6** the Johnson County Post is hosting its general election candidate forum. **WHEN:****Tuesday, October 6
6:00 p.m. Commission Districts 1 & 5****7:00 p.m. Chair****WHERE:
Central Resource Library
**9875 W. 87th Street, Overland ParkThe event is **free and open to the public.** The Johnson County Post builds its forum questions from input submitted by local residents, so this is an opportunity to hear directly from us on the issues Johnson County voters are asking about.Property taxes. County spending. Growth. Housing. Development. Transparency. The role and priorities of the next County Chair.You have heard a lot of claims throughout this campaign. Good news, folks:

Donald Trump just lost at the Supreme Court, thanks in part to California's defense of mail-in voting.

A few weeks ago, the Court rejected the Trump Administration's latest attempt to restrict mail-in voting.

for the people who already have the most.

None of that is negotiable, but none of it happens if we lose our seats.

There's a reason the same forces keep lining up against us every cycle —
the MAGA extremists, the corporations, the dark money, the folks in our
own party who'd rather we just fell in line.

with the people who show up, support how and when they can, because they
know what we’ve built is worth protecting. That's a movement that doesn't
leave people behind.

together. And right now, ahead of tonight’s deadline, we need that same
energy.
