The air in El Jefe Cafe was thick enough to chew, like the crab cakes some monster was devouring right in my shot frame. Congressman Gus Bilirakis stood there, microphone in hand, not selling but pleading, begging the eight true believers to stay with the President. Things would get better next year, he promised. The war with Iran had to happen. Classified intelligence. Things above our pay grade. Trump was fighting for us. Hold the line.
Twenty bodies in the room if you counted the campaign vultures, Libertarian and Republican candidates watching each other like hawks. Strip them away and you had eight old souls clustered in what was supposed to look like a movement. I didn't work the room this time. I sat and shot it, capturing the whole layout. Especially Brian Lambert, one of the alternatives I'd been watching in this race. The state of a room is always in the faces, not the speeches.
A woman who'd driven back to Tampa from some state I forgot, came up to me and began telling me how she was trying to get back into the political game. Crossed the country for a room this size. We talked the way people do at these things when the speeches are still warming up and when you are trying to make connections in an unfamiliar room. We spoke about where she'd been, why she came back, what she thought this room still was. Once the program started the banter died.
That's when the crab-cake monster sat down across from me. Mouth open. Lips wet. Smacking his way through those seafood grenades like some kind of goddamn torture. I gave him a look that could curdle milk. He didn't see it in my eyes, and if he did then he made a deliberate choice to continue with his open-mouthed assault. He kept chewing. Oblivious to my camera, and he ruined the footage. That was the room. Not a packed hall of patriots. Eight old souls, a woman who'd crossed the country to start over, a plate of crab cakes, and a congressman asking them to stay loyal to Trump.
After enough months on the trail, you can tell a pitch from a plea. A pitch assumes the room is already with you and asks for a little more. A plea assumes the room is leaving. Bilirakis was pleading. Standing there, I realized the most revealing thing about the speech wasn't anything he said. It was that he felt he had to say it at all, to a room this size, six weeks before an election.
After the speeches from all the candidates the only one that stood out to me was the NPA candidate for the Mayor of Tampa. She spoke about having Republican roots but finally leaving because she was betrayed by that party in a previous election. I went straight to her, finally leaving the mess left behind by the crab-cake man. I wanted to get her take on our city's infrastructure mess. She's been a regular at all city and county meetings. Right in the middle of my conversation I felt someone from behind grab my arm. It was a Republican nominee in Hillsborough who came over to talk to me.
I remember his primary. He didn't have the President's endorsement. What he had was the theater of it. Photos. Grip-and-grins. Thumbs up. The feed stacked with pictures of himself next to the man. All the little tricks you run when you need primary voters to believe Trump is for you and you don't have the tweet that says so. Ask someone in August what he stood for and they'd have pointed at the picture.
If you were to look now, the pictures are gone. The gallery is not what it was. The frames look like they were cleaned for a different race. Like a campaign washing off yesterday's message before meeting tomorrow's voters.
During our conversation I had mentioned that another campaign had been trying to reach non-MAGA Republicans, and I asked the honest question: how do you even find them? There's no box on the voter file for that.
He said something to the effect that if he could find them, he would win this race.
I won't stretch that line farther than it can go. A passing remark. A small room. But follow who said it and when. This is the man who just won a Republican primary in Florida by a wide margin by looking like the Trump guy. Now the general is in front of him, and the voters he's thinking about are the Republicans who never wore the hat. The primary was about proving you belonged to the movement. The general, apparently, is about finding the people who never did.
THEN THERE WAS THE STAFFER, a man from the nominee's campaign. I won't name him. He's a staffer, not a candidate, and I doubt he thought he was talking to someone who writes things down. What he said stuck harder than anything else that night.
He said out loud what most candidates won't. The war. The economy. The whole direction. Trump had lied, he said. Trump was looking out for himself. Trump had sold out the voters who put him there.
This wasn't some Democrat heckling from the parking lot. This was someone inside the operation of a Republican nominee for Congress, at a patriot event, saying the President betrayed his own base. At the front of the room, Bilirakis was asking everyone to keep faith with that same President.
Those are the three men, one room. The congressman asking the room to remain loyal. The nominee looking past the movement that nominated him. The staffer saying what seems to be a growing trend from campaigns. Same party. Same night. No two agreed.
I walked out into the Florida heat feeling like I'd seen a crack in a dam, and I knew there was more water coming.
IF THIS WERE ONE STRANGE NIGHT in Hillsborough County it would be a curiosity. It's not. Look at the primaries. The whole season was Trump. Every forum. Every mailer. Every qualifying-period billboard. Are you with him or not. That was the product.
One time candidate for congress in District 11, Anthony Sabatini, spent months going after the President. The war with Iran. The rest of the agenda. A known critic, not a quiet one. Then qualifying approached and the pictures went up. Him and Trump. Roadside. Mail. The implied sentence was the same one every other Republican was selling: this man is the Trump choice. He didn't have the endorsement. Trump's operation sent a cease-and-desist telling the PAC behind the ads to stop using the name and face. The point isn't that Sabatini got caught. The point is that even a man who had been attacking the President still needed the photograph to get on the field. Put it up when you need the base. Take the letter when the campaign lawyers show up. Drop it when the general starts and the base is no longer the whole electorate. Exploit, then silence.
NBC News counted at least a dozen Republican candidates putting distance between themselves and the President. The kind of self-preservation that would have been unimaginable for most of the last decade. The numbers are sliding. Inflation is grinding. The Iran war is making it worse. Decision Desk HQ puts Democrats' odds of taking the House at 70 percent.
Look at the governor's race. Byron Donalds, as Trump-aligned as anyone in this state, cut eight references to Trump's support off his campaign website. Photo of Donalds and his wife with the President: gone. Section on implementing the Trump agenda: gone. The word at the top of his priority list now is affordability, a term the President has mocked in public. Donalds says it's not distancing. His team had been reworking the site for two months, he says, to focus on general-election issues. Fine. Nobody rebuilds a homepage to take the President off it unless something about the campaign's calculation has changed.
Down in Miami, Congresswoman Maria Elvira Salazar skipped the quiet edit and looked into a camera. She told the President that some Hispanic voters feel betrayed by immigration enforcement she said has gone too far. The same tension I had just watched play out in Hillsborough.
It's not everywhere. I won't pretend it is. In Texas, in the newly drawn districts, some Republican candidates are still running the President in their ads because he still pulls there. That matters too. The performance changes where the audience changes.
HERE'S WHAT DOESN'T LET ME SLEEP. It's the question I would put to every Republican on the ballot this fall.
In the primary the test was loyalty. I lived it. Every forum. Every endorsement conversation. Every mailer. Same question: are you with him or not? The candidates who won mostly won by answering loudest. The nominee in that room answered it with pictures when he didn't have the endorsement. That was the product on offer.
Six weeks later some of those same winners are scrubbing the name and hunting for voters who never bought the product. So which version did the primary voters nominate? The man who needed to look like the movement, or the man now running on affordability and hoping nobody brings up the President?
A primary voter has every right to ask that. So does a general-election voter trying to decide whether the person asking for their vote in November is the same person who will be voting in Washington in January.
Bilirakis told the room things would get better next year. Maybe he's right. I noticed the people with the most to lose on November 3rd weren't standing next to him when he said it.
**Your voice is your crown.**
**Gavriel Soriano**
**Every One A King**

If you’re reading this, you know how much is at stake.
Republicans have launched unprecedented efforts to manipulate maps and weaken voting power across the country. And right now, a slew of anti-democracy candidates are running in critical state-level races nationwide. If elected, they will use the same GOP playbook to threaten fair maps and fair representation.
Our strategy to fight back is expansive, because we don’t have any other choice if we want to defend democracy with everything we’ve got. Falling short of our fundraising goal now — with only one full month before the midterms — means having to make difficult choices on where and how we can support our over 300+ Democracy Defenders.
We don’t want to have to make tough decisions about where to pull back in the final weeks of this election. We chose these priority state-level races based on their direct impacts on map drawing, map approval, and map interpretations. | | Dear Peter,

I just wanted to send you a quick reminder that **tonight at midnight** is the deadline for [contributions](https://us.list-manage.com/16kxoUQ9Y1I?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to appear on the next and final financial report in my campaign for re-election as Nevada Controller.

I also want to extend a big THANK YOU to all of you who responded to my email a couple days ago with a contribution. The response was amazing, and if you were among those who contributed, then please just accept this email as a token of my gratitude.

But if you didn’t get a chance to contribute, I hope you’ll consider doing so today. As I mentioned in my last email, every single dollar we raise from here on out will go directly into my voter-contact effort.

[You can contribute by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/qKDtgl_MQIP?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

If you haven’t seen it yet, [here is the TV ad](https://us.list-manage.com/wjhR9LA_W6n?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) we’ve been running for a couple weeks now. We’ve been getting a really great response to the ad, and your support today will help make sure we get my message in front of the critical voters who are going to determine the outcome of this race!

Again, if you’ve contributed just recently, then please simply accept my deepest thanks for your generous support. But if you haven’t had the chance to, then I hope I can count on you before midnight tonight.

Thank you so much!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

Fellow American,
I understand that you get spammed with a whole lot of emails and texts from Republicans, especially in these final weeks of the midterms, so I try to avoid sending them whenever possible.
[When you see my name on your phone, I want you to know it’s about something that actually matters.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=9d2b41108feb4dba8a6b78062a3a5eca&_e=K3XLASM9hrpWPt4FNGI-Agxjdxtk42O6PgiaEImnGv31RZ8atJTuTc0-pe8vX-iXvkHc5aDvnOUP5btDLWpHUCarhxbxpFjZYrW2VZ76eA1_1SnyDb77_duhUuetiWeiUeelNxlU7estxiann8YSG-OyT58nrzCelB1CdzDplPb24rYOZZbFLTN9LuQKjWg6h1Rge_KIEzo6YAuA6PoCvd106qv4G6bzjYPJPYSUwRz3S5dNlOWkm_WholbGnXlhOMUTFJ6hUk2UaVbdjo8lM77b71pIQ36YGY3BFL93iH6eAbq3r_g2qQGur9lrCk_JGgyuctxKj-bHUFZWVGJ12_ACvG33S5f3rj3eBxaxtom2ZnvjRgqxsCljHMwj_cZCqj_gLf7cbwWweV7fSDZcx2r6WTdtazPLO_-Z44jWsMcV6qLjnIVYfzS3WinkDkiT4_kSK44MjxURsEjKQi9wo_5m6TzJRl9BRnNlbg8-3wifrDp1_VBbYGR577XiLbZT-oP9lwl1kfzzZ1SzrnfkCvH88P8FtkA_5ebV5_bPse78WSX5BiI78pEWZ6Di2y39ieQV2fkzfSuW7ZMxXXeIDOb1oFRGF17gU8d8J5CrOnScRdv7Qudu8QQW3oq6vAF_7btgAckgLSFYpvA0uYJpFae0txw2hZJdFEPy3esKX9jHmPTkJBSs2s-cD29SmkQ2RW1O1_O4pcclc9tmbSaSf_Xjb3OAxlh6magmuyd6wZ2Vyp2vG0SlsI8QrbwtKBsKAcyojoSxGMBXdK_CRgc1Rgz5on0CJDDNJG_uQb05-YBcY2q6TwZpCvQYAtngobq-KhaX1WU8wR9E85YY7sxGOWr2NYGpnJoxHIWimksateBs9n18uKV_I0qVrG1fYaGD979Em_4flkXgqcwL_-BTuApGq62J1Fkpijl-WyWLczA%3D)
Well, this might just be the single most important message I've ever written!
But because of that, I'm under pressure to make every word count - and honestly, it's really hard to find the right words to convey the scale of the threat facing America.
At this point, I've re-written this letter several times, and ultimately, I decided to just write to you straight from my heart with words inspired by my unwavering faith in God and our Country.
There are no media consultants or comms people changing my words or watering down my thoughts. This all comes straight from [ME](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=9d2b41108feb4dba8a6b78062a3a5eca&_e=K3XLASM9hrpWPt4FNGI-Agxjdxtk42O6PgiaEImnGv31RZ8atJTuTc0-pe8vX-iXvkHc5aDvnOUP5btDLWpHUCarhxbxpFjZYrW2VZ76eA1_1SnyDb77_duhUuetiWeiUeelNxlU7estxiann8YSG-OyT58nrzCelB1CdzDplPb24rYOZZbFLTN9LuQKjWg6h1Rge_KIEzo6YAuA6PoCvd106qv4G6bzjYPJPYSUwRz3S5dNlOWkm_WholbGnXlhOMUTFJ6hUk2UaVbdjo8lM77b71pIQ36YGY3BFL93iH6eAbq3r_g2qQGur9lrCk_JGgyuctxKj-bHUFZWVGJ12_ACvG33S5f3rj3eBxaxtolYJorfDsancmS2VccRHHnPNBA_Lq-_ZCNAcPA_ZCSXpyVTz_azi_dyzsd9aTC-OGm9PtLMik64PqKQ6QVfolcgh9dZzQKubm1GZ9XLyaXVq6FnjK5Polu54IYj7eVcBTkVcOEMI6J9_BaHFxiUtZUsheqSBmYX7c8SqCkukeBG4QPXeFjM9g8TJk0P5mF6pB9k3hZj-hix0L7Oyw1r_vjaE6P0YMNZLFOwsfe0FBUhoqw1ijbYXjSaSPwALlAvXgscBJNbOt7iIX_abXXIc382nHIHxDEmHTVCO-3uFuWjHxrG4zKI9rStVUqHUA4HR-S8OEno1YFfdjs57AyOTeerMjx4-Kynaqbdu2Xyy1Y39dZkobMELGCJCEecJIwxZHYwBXXxxBn7tNt4aP3yDoKzU-inKQjNuoSBOfRdKGvmmccWQE9CxvDhiPCfV_iCvaH8SjR0EJmT4oDI3TAb1-E01WPQXh568cbcB36edFaZqFBzVzEsFW4isLEWgheEKoehexD7iyn8mgcRt_wjXQads9J8Zbx4sRnesvu2RoWluR0LPCOBegPM_RFtc0TiznA%3D), so I apologize if it's a bit rough around the edges.
I'm not repeating the same worn-out talking points you're probably used to!
Look - I know the mainstream media is downplaying it, but the Democrat Party is getting more and more extreme, to the point that I believe they pose a threat to our free Republic.

clean_body: Every word comes straight from my heart. | Fellow American, I understand that you get spammed with a whole lot of emails and texts from Republicans, especially in these final weeks of the midterms, so I try to avoid sending them whenever possible. Well, this might just be the single most important message I've ever written! But because of that, I'm under pressure to make every word count - and honestly, it's really hard to find the right words to convey the scale of the threat facing America. At this point, I've re-written this letter several times, and ultimately, I decided to just write to you straight from my heart with words inspired by my unwavering faith in God and our Country. There are no media consultants or comms people changing my words or watering down my thoughts. This all comes straight from , so I apologize if it's a bit rough around the edges. I'm not repeating the same worn-out talking points you're probably used to! Look - I know the mainstream media is downplaying it, but the Democrat Party is getting more and more extreme, to the point that I believe they pose a threat to our free Republic. They're embracing Communists, pro-Sharia candidates, and all kinds of radical Leftists who HATE conservatives, Christians, and the very values that made our country great. There was a time not too long ago when American voters would punish this kind of extremism at the ballot box. But instead, polling shows the Democrats are SURGING to their largest ever lead - - in the final weeks of the election! How are they winning in the polls? It's certainly not because American voters suddenly support radical ideas like communism, open borders, and defunding the police. A lot of elected officials aren't willing to say this, but I will... The left hates you, they hate your vote, and they hate MAGA for putting America First! Right now, they're spending to fully verify that new electorate to ensure that every last Democrat voter (illegals too!) casts a ballot in November. At the end of the day, winning the midterms is a simple numbers game, and as it stands, the American people still have the upper hand on the Left. 2024 proved that decisively! But our advantage disappears the second Republicans stop showing up to vote... We need to verify that every Republican voter - especially - will show up to cast a ballot on or before November 3rd. If Republicans don't turn out and we LOSE the midterms, the consequences for our country will be downright catastrophic. Jack Smith didn't have to show up yesterday.
Let me say that again. He did not have to be there. He's a private citizen. He's already been threatened with prosecution by the same administration he investigated. He could have fought the subpoena. He could have lawyered up and stayed home. A lot of people in his position would have.
He showed up anyway. He sat in that chair for four hours. He told the truth. Under oath. In that building. In front of the people who have been lying about him for years.
That's good trouble. That's what standing your ground looks like.
And what did Republicans bring to meet him?
Basketball.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Tl3WU0Gtd42bzzhK0U6O-tWxswgnVGlyep_mwMqpGH4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=218233247)
Senator Eric Schmitt of Missouri stood up and accused Jack Smith of perjury. He said Smith had lied under oath about attending an Atlanta Hawks game in 2024. He was ready. He had his moment. He had his clip.
There was one problem. The game wasn't an Atlanta Hawks game. It was an Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball game. Different team. Different sport. Different city. Different everything.
A United States senator tried to catch a former federal prosecutor in a perjury trap and couldn't tell the Hawks from the Hawkeyes. And when this was pointed out, Schmitt said he made no mistake.
This is who these people are. This is what they've got.
I watched Jack Smith sit in that room and I felt something I haven't felt in a while. I felt proud. Because I know what it costs to walk into that building and tell the truth when powerful people want you to shut up. I've done it. I testified before Congress about what I saw on January 6th while members of that same Congress tried to make me the story. I know what it feels like to sit in that chair while people who were on the wrong side of history look you in the eye and call you a liar.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e95d50d-5fdb-4daf-bf74-50cc40e76ee2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jack Smith looked back at every single one of them and didn't move an inch.
He said he wouldn't be silenced by threats of prosecution. He said his team proved beyond reasonable doubt that Donald Trump engaged in serious crimes. He said the strongest witnesses in his case, the people who were the difference between the rule of law holding and not, were Republicans.
He said that. In the Capitol. In their faces. Yesterday.
And Chuck Grassley, who has spent two years telling anyone who would listen that the investigation was politically motivated, sat there and accused Smith of partisanship. This is the same Chuck Grassley whose party voted against certifying a free and fair election. The same party that called the people who attacked us "hostages" and "patriots" and fought to pardon every single one of them. These people have the nerve to sit across from Jack Smith and lecture him about partisanship.
I'm done pretending this is a normal political disagreement. It is not. These are people who watched January 6th happen, some of them helped make it happen, and they have spent five years trying to rewrite it. They pardoned the people who beat my colleagues. They shut down the investigations. They dismissed the cases. They threatened the prosecutors. And when the last person willing to tell the truth showed up and sat down in that chair, the best they could do was accuse him of lying about a basketball game and get the teams wrong.
Jack Smith said something in that hearing I've been sitting with. He said he wishes he had spoken up more. He came from a school of prosecution where you let the work speak. You stay quiet. You don't respond to attacks. You trust the record.
He said that was a mistake.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Tl3WU0Gtd42bzzhK0U6O-tWxswgnVGlyep_mwMqpGH4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=218233247)
"There are things being put out daily that are patently untrue, and you know they're untrue," he said. "People can unfairly malign your team and your case in a way that you really can't respond to."
He's right. I learned that too. Silence gives liars room to fill. And these liars have been filling that room for five years.
The pardons happened. The dismissed cases are real. The DOJ that is now running interference for Trump instead of investigating him is real. Nothing yesterday undoes any of that.
But Jack Smith showed up anyway. He told the truth anyway. On the record. Under oath. In that building.
I was in that building on January 6th. I held the line that day so that building could keep working. Yesterday Jack Smith walked back in and did his part.
That's the kind of American hero we don't make enough noise about. Not the ones who do the easy thing. The ones who show up when it's hard, when there's nothing left to win, when the people across the table are lying to your face, and they tell the truth anyway.

-Harry

| We file our final numbers for the quarter at midnight tonight, but before we do I wanted to say thank you.

clean_body: | | Peter, The October sprint is nearly here. This is the month when the close races turn into flipped seats, and we're in a great position. James Talarico is ahead in the polling and electrifying the top of the ticket. Our own polling has us in a strong position to defeat Keith Self with new voters joining this movement every day. The national picture is even better. The Kansas Senate seat is in play for the first time since the Dust Bowl. And Midwest GOP pollsters just briefed their own lawmakers that seats favoring the GOP by 15 points now fall inside the margin of error. The local and national tailwinds are there. And this is the team ready to turn those tailwinds into a sure thing. | These folks have knocked doors through triple-digit summers and planted signs from the suburbs to the fence lines, and every community in between. We will spend every day of October leaving nothing to chance. Momentum does not finish the job. People do, and ours are the hardest-working campaigners in Texas. Hey Peter,
---
It’s crunch time, and things are looking promising for this election in November. We’ve seen how unpopular the president has become in our district because his policies continue to harm our wallets every day. I mean, gas is over 4 dollars a gallon ... and diesel fuel is over 6 dollars. Our current representative is a rubber stamp for the president. On every vote, he continues to fall in line with the party, regardless of what that means for the people in NC-13. We need an independent voice in Congress who will stand up to party bosses and think for our community. body:
Join us to reach Pennsylvania voters, recruit volunteers, and build our collective power before November 3. | |
---
Peter, **Working people have the power to change who governs this country. We build that power when we organize our neighbors, bring new people into the movement, and turn the demands of our communities into action. With less than 5 weeks until Election Day, we need you in that work.** OnePA members know what it means to fight for schools that have what our children need, hospitals that stay open, communities with clean air to breathe, and an economy where working families can afford to live. We organize because the people making decisions about our lives must answer to the communities living with the consequences. **On Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays, we’re calling voters in Pennsylvania’s swing congressional districts to help flip Congress blue. On the other phonebank days, we’re calling voters across Pennsylvania to recruit volunteers.** Together, we’re growing the team that can reach more people and make our communities heard this November. That is how organizing grows. Someone picks up the phone, has a conversation, and invites another person to take action. A voter becomes a volunteer. That volunteer reaches more people. We build the relationships and collective strength to win elections and keep pressing our demands after Election Day. body:
The FEC deadline is midnight tonight - contribute what you can now!
| | | | Hi Friend,
Suhas doesn't have a plan to balance the federal budget. **I do, a real, 3-step path to get it done in 11 years.**
Suhas didn't stand up to defend against extremism in his own party when he had the chance. **I will, every single time, left or right.**
Suhas voted against keeping the government funded, 7 times. **I never will betray the federal workforce like that.**
Suhas had ten years of warning on the data center crisis and six years in office to do something about it.**I won't wait for an election to act.**
Suhas voted no on getting money out of politics, and no on real tax relief for working families.**I'll _always_ fight for both.**
**VA-10 deserves a congressman who leads, not one who reacts.**
---
[HELP ELECT A LEADER TO CONGRESS](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
**Here's the truth: talk doesn't win elections, action does.**
Right now, at this very moment, we are almost 12 hours away from a deadline that will show the entire country whether VA-10 is ready to fight back, or whether we let Suhas coast to victory on excuses and empty promises.
I am not asking you to sit this one out. I am asking you to show up, right now, before this window closes for good.
**$25. $50. $100. Whatever you can give, give it tonight.**
Before this deadline slams shut and this opportunity is gone.
This is the moment, and you don't want to watch from the sidelines. Join our team and get in the fight to restore faith in the American Dream!
[FUEL THE FIGHT FOR THE AMERICAN DREAM](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
| | | God bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

| When my family first came to Denver, we didn't have much.
My parents were working multiple jobs while my dad made his way through pharmacy school, and money was tight.
What we did have was a community.
Family and friends helped with babysitting when my parents were at work. They helped with groceries and passed along job leads. When our family was struggling, somebody stepped in and carried part of the load.
Before long, my parents were doing the same for other families.
That's one of the earliest lessons I learned about what a community can look like.
You do what you can, you take care of the people around you, and when enough people each carry a small piece, suddenly the impossible starts to feel manageable.
That idea has stayed with me throughout this campaign.
From the beginning, we chose to build this around people rather than corporate PACs. That means the work has depended on thousands of individual choices, volunteers knocking doors, neighbors talking to neighbors, people making calls, sharing information, and helping us stay connected to communities across Denver.
As we head into October, that work becomes even more visible.
Ballots will soon arrive, and voters will decide on candidates and ballot measures that will shape Denver and this country long after this election is over. Our job is to keep showing up, keep listening, and keep making sure people have the information they need to participate.
[Tonight at midnight is our last quarterly FEC deadline before November. clean_body: I've been thinking about the community that raised me | | | | | == | When my family first came to Denver, we didn't have much. My parents were working multiple jobs while my dad made his way through pharmacy school, and money was tight. What we did have was a community. Family and friends helped with babysitting when my parents were at work. They helped with groceries and passed along job leads. When our family was struggling, somebody stepped in and carried part of the load. Before long, my parents were doing the same for other families. That's one of the earliest lessons I learned about what a community can look like. You do what you can, you take care of the people around you, and when enough people each carry a small piece, suddenly the impossible starts to feel manageable. That idea has stayed with me throughout this campaign. From the beginning, we chose to build this around people rather than corporate PACs. That means the work has depended on thousands of individual choices, volunteers knocking doors, neighbors talking to neighbors, people making calls, sharing information, and helping us stay connected to communities across Denver. As we head into October, that work becomes even more visible. Ballots will soon arrive, and voters will decide on candidates and ballot measures that will shape Denver and this country long after this election is over. I've served this country in uniform. **$18.59.** That’s the average contribution to my campaign. And I couldn’t be prouder. In Washington, campaigns are built around PAC contributions, lobbyist money, and ultra-wealthy donors writing massive checks. That also means they’re beholden to these donors' special interests and policy initiatives. But I’ve chosen a different path. I don’t take money from billionaires, PACs, or lobbyists, and I never will–because I won’t owe my agenda to the people who can afford to write the biggest checks. Instead, this campaign is built around thousands of people giving what they can. On Tuesday, September 22, Vice President JD Vance announced that his fraud task force was removing 750,000 fake Obamacare recipients from the Market. An additional 419,000 recipients are also being investigated for suspected fraud. The removal will save taxpayers roughly $2.2 billion, in an effort to remove scammers from receiving benefits from the Affordable Care Act.
"We're doing an amazing and common sense thing- We're making sure that the people receiving Obamacare subsidies are actually entitled to receive them," said Vance. "We weren't doing that before."
According to Vance, the Biden administration had been providing incentives for brokers to enroll individuals into the Obamacare system while simultaneously easing eligibility requirements for the system. Government officials were not checking whether or not individuals met requirements, meaning that the financial incentive was encouraged by Biden-era apathy.
Shortly after Vance announced the removal of hundreds of thousands of Obamacare recipients, stocks **[plummeted](https://substack.com/redirect/753a7b0b-f0b2-40ac-8564-542600124de7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** among several of the program's leading health insurance sellers. Oscar Health, which has nearly 3 million health plans primarily enrolled in Obamacare, saw their stock price fall more than 4%. Centene, which has 3.5 million enrolled in the Market, saw their stock prices drop by almost 3%.

Many health insurance companies engaged in the Market have seen dips in enrollment, but have alleged that this is not due to fraud, but because the Trump administration has not expanded subsidies to make Obamacare more affordable.
Vance stated that his fraud task force would now begin conducting an additional verification process for those enrolled in Obamacare. They are planning to confirm whether they are legal American residents who meet the income requirements necessary to receive benefits.
The task force allegedly found a ring of 40 brokers who had fraudulently siphoned roughly 50,000 people into Obamacare, including many illegal immigrants. "To put into context the amount of money that we're stopping from going to fraudsters today, $2.2 billion, the average American child receives about $4,000 in health care benefits every single year," **[said](https://substack.com/redirect/481d05ca-73ed-4a7c-b776-8571f802a4d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Vance. "That means that we are saving 550,000 American children's worth of healthcare that was going to fraudsters."
Since the inception of Vance's task force, the **[largest](https://substack.com/redirect/e1739dd5-892a-408f-aaad-36e680da4f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e1739dd5-892a-408f-aaad-36e680da4f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[proportion](https://substack.com/redirect/e1739dd5-892a-408f-aaad-36e680da4f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of fraud and corruption among government programs has been found in the Department of Health and Human Services. | As a Navy SEAL veteran, I spent my life defending the freedoms that make America exceptional.
Results matter. In the General Assembly I passed bills every year where every Democrat and every Republican voted yes.
Now I'm continuing that mission in Congress for Virginia's 5th District.
My Democrat opponent, Tom Perriello is pretending to be a moderate and is trying to trick you just like Spanberger and Mamdani. He is a radical leftist who was just endorsed by socialist AOC because he supports her agenda. He worked for George Soros and helped run his Open Society Foundation. He supports the job-killing climate change agenda of cap-and-trade, has dismissed the NRA as a "nut job extremist organization," and cast the deciding vote for the unaffordable Obamacare disaster.
While my democrat opponent has spent his career advancing progressive causes, my team and I have delivered real results for Virginia's 5th:

* Successfully worked with Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao to secure Navy and Marine Corps ROTC for Liberty University, a goal pursued since 1971
* Passed two bills out of the House with bipartisan support, including the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act that the previous six VA 05 congressmen failed to advance even through subcommittee over 25 years
* Returned more than $10 million owed by the federal government to people in our district
* Helped negotiate $20 billion in investment for the district, including the Avio groundbreaking in Hurt just yesterday
* Worked with Rubio and Hegseth to help 57 constituents from a Charlottesville church return home safely from Israel during ballistic missile attacks

We are just getting started.
This is the clear choice: proven leadership and constitutional values versus a radical progressive activist who instinctively prefers to support a riot rather than work hard to solve a problem.
Tonight is the deadline.
Please stand with me before midnight and make the strongest contribution you can. Every dollar fuels the final push to win Virginia's 5th District and send a clear message that we will not surrender our freedoms.
Don't forget to get friends to vote by November 3rd. Thank you for your prayers, dedication, generosity, and unwavering faith in our cause. I look forward to continuing this journey with you.

I’m no stranger to being underestimated, Peter.

It’s Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17035?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Flanagan-Underdog_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=3279%2E259176%2ERJD1zM) As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. _And I proved them wrong._ [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17035?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Flanagan-Underdog_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=5&akid=3279%2E259176%2ERJD1zM) When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. _I proved the doubters wrong._ [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17035?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.30_Flanagan-Underdog_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=6&akid=3279%2E259176%2ERJD1zM) In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and _proved the doubters wrong._

So now, when I hear folks say we can’t compete with the avalanche of GOP cash coming our way I know that we will do what we always do, _we’re going to prove the doubters wrong,_ _again._

There will always be doubters, but I’ve always chosen not to listen. I keep my head down, get the work done, and deliver for the people of Minnesota. When a working family sits down at the kitchen table to pay the bills, they don't think about fraud. They think about the rent, the copay, the grocery total, the tuition installment. They don't connect those numbers to a phony day-care center in Minneapolis or a ghost hospice patient in Los Angeles. They should. A slice of nearly every bill ordinary Americans pay is what we might call the fraud tax -- the cost of theft, priced into the system and passed along to the honest.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b68bce48-c21e-47b2-9754-cf192ee2b487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Start with the scale. Justice Department officials now estimate that health care fraud alone drains on the order of $300 billion a year -- a sum comparable to the entire annual budget of the Department of Veterans Affairs. In June 2025, the department announced the largest health care fraud takedown in its history: nearly 200 federal cases, $14.6 billion in intended losses, defendants accused of billing Medicare for surgeries never performed, drugs never dispensed, and hospice care for patients who weren't dying. By January 2026, the administration had to stand up an entirely new Justice Department division for national fraud enforcement -- because, prosecutors will tell you plainly, the old machinery was built for a problem a fraction of this size.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.z4gnrXHeaHFofnynNaNpgEQpgNVDtxo6RoTtzpsqqU4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=215370337)
Minnesota became the national cautionary tale. Federal prosecutors have said fraud in state-run programs there could top $9 billion. The Feeding Our Future case alone -- stolen school-lunch money laundered through fake food sites -- put 78 people under indictment, has produced 57 convictions so far, and drained $250 million or more from child nutrition programs. Prosecutors have alleged that half or more of the roughly $18 billion in Medicaid funds that flowed through fourteen Minnesota-run programs since 2018 may have been stolen -- and Governor Walz himself has allowed that a $1 billion estimate for day-care-sector fraud "could be accurate." In May 2026 came still another wave: fifteen defendants, some $90 million in alleged theft across seven programs -- child care assistance, early-learning subsidies, housing stabilization, autism therapy. A day-care center that exists mostly on paper. An autism provider billing for therapy never delivered. A "housing stabilization" company with no housing to stabilize.
Then came the housing-and-immigration dimension. Operation Twin Shield, a federal immigration-fraud investigation centered on the Twin Cities, uncovered what investigators described as widespread fraud in status and benefits applications. Federal mortgage-fraud probes followed in Minneapolis, where local brokers now warn that the enforcement push could chill spring homebuying, and HUD moved to restrict FHA-backed mortgages for non-permanent residents. Whatever one's politics, the economics are blunt: straw buyers, inflated appraisals, and fraudulent loans don't just steal from lenders. They corrupt the comparable sales appraisers use to value an honest family's house, they raise the loss assumptions lenders bake into every mortgage, and they invite blanket crackdowns that tighten credit for everyone -- including the lawful immigrant families who did nothing wrong. Higher taxable assessments, higher insurance rates, larger estate taxes...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c313056-7412-41b1-8766-7350737d3c67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
note St Louis Fed discontinued (2019-12-12)
How does theft become an unaffordable price? Four ways. First, stolen federal money doesn't vanish; it is financed by Treasury borrowing, and the interest is paid by taxpayers. Second, fraud inflates the utilization data on which reimbursement formulas are built -- bill enough phantom home-health visits and hospice stays, and program actuaries raise their cost projections, which surfaces as higher premiums, higher payroll taxes, or trimmed benefits. Third, fraud demands defensive overhead: re-verification of every Medicaid provider in Minnesota under threat of a federal payment freeze, more auditors, more compliance staff -- and those costs are charged back into the system. Fourth, fraud destroys trust, and lost trust tightens eligibility for everyone. The mother who genuinely needs child-care assistance now faces a gauntlet designed around the scammers.
The United States federal government allocated approximately $4.6 trillion to $5.2 trillion in total funding to respond to and recover from the COVID-19 pandemic. Globally, estimated total recovery and fiscal stimulus measures by governments exceeded $14 trillion.**** Government watchdogs and investigations estimate that at least $280 billion to over $400 billion in COVID-19 relief funds were lost to fraud and theft, with broader estimates of potential waste and fraud combined exceeding $420 billion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f44aad84-c1e5-463c-a22c-8ea622ef4429?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The same pattern repeats across the programs I have covered for months. Hospice -- meant for the dying -- has become a growth industry for crooks, from the billion-dollar California billing schemes to the Los Angeles takedown prosecutors called Operation Never Say Die. USDA's own estimates put SNAP trafficking at roughly a billion dollars a year. In higher education, investigators have broken up rings of "Pell runners" who enroll straw students, pocket the grant refunds, and disappear. Every dollar stolen from a food program, a college grant, or a deathbed benefit is a dollar that forces Congress to choose: raise the cost, cut the benefit, or tighten the door. Ordinary families lose in all three directions -- and the people already at the margins lose first.
Nowhere is that last point more painful than among our veterans. After a decade of genuine progress that cut veteran homelessness by more than half, the single-night counts jumped by roughly seven percent two years running -- recent federal counts found more than 32,000 veterans homeless on a single January night. These are men and women who survived combat and lost the peace at home, in an economy where rents have outrun fixed disability checks and pensions. VA care and housing programs cost the country well over $300 billion a year -- the same order of magnitude as what health care fraud alone is estimated to drain. That is the arithmetic of the fraud tax: every phantom hospice patient and paper day-care center is a claim on the same Treasury that funds a veteran's housing voucher, his copay assistance, his hospice bed. Fraud doesn't just compete with veterans' care -- in a budget that must balance politically if not legally, it crowds it out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c8a6766-cf46-4da5-a827-dc5fd9f06153?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
None of this is abstract to the veteran standing at a VA clinic door with a copay he can't cover, or sleeping in a car outside a shelter that's full. And none of it is anti-immigrant, whatever the loudest voices on cable news claim -- the victims include lawful immigrant business owners tarred by the schemes and honest beneficiaries whose benefits get frozen while investigators clean house. The fight is against thieves, and it is a fight we must win: prosecution and restitution, yes, but also eligibility verification, payment freezes for crooked providers, and transparency about where every federal dollar goes.
The measure of a country is how it treats those who served and those who cannot fend for themselves. Right now, we are asking them to pay a tax they never voted for -- the fraud tax -- while the people who stole from them buy boats and build towers with the proceeds. That is not America the Beautiful. It is America the ransacked. And it stays that way until the honest majority decides it won't be.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/314b40b8-7434-421a-bbee-66db7393e940?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Good afternoon, Peter. Tonight is deadline night, and tomorrow my team will start to prepare our public FEC report, which has information on how much we’ve raised and from how many donors. It’s critical that we show that we have the resources to run a competitive campaign. New York is an expensive state to run in – and our opponent, Mike Lawler, has a big leg up over us in terms of money. But forget about that for a moment. I want to talk about why I’m in this race to begin with. I was a junior in high school on 9/11 when the Twin Towers fell. The next day, I began my West Point application. After graduating, I did six overseas deployments serving in combat zones like Iraq and Afghanistan. I did that out of a love for this country. Back then, I never thought that the greatest threat to America’s future would come from within our own borders. But the people running this administration do not share our values – or the values of the generations of Americans who fought and sacrificed to make this country better. **So I made the decision to run for Congress, again, out of love for this country.** My opponent, Mike Lawler, has become a rubber stamp for Trump and the MAGA agenda. Our campaign has a clear path to beating him and flipping this seat. But it’s going to be a tough fight. So please. **(RADIO MONOLOGUE)**
**[THEME MUSIC FADES UNDER]**
Okay, settle in, folks. Grab your artisanal popcorn--actually, wait. Check the bag first. Make sure it actually contains popcorn and not, say, just shredded wheat with ambition. Because we need to talk about avocado oil. The miracle elixir. The darling of every health podcast, every paleo CrossFit mom, every guy in your office who brings a salad in a glass container and makes you feel bad about your sandwich. We were told it was good fat. We were told it was worth twelve dollars a bottle. We were told... a lot of things.
Turns out, we were told lies.
Quick side note:
Avocados have earned the nickname "green gold" because the dense, creamy fruit generates profit margins that rival precious metals, but beneath the glossy piles of Hass avocados at your neighborhood grocery lies a supply chain increasingly shaped by cartel violence and monopoly control. In Michoacan, Mexico--the heart of global avocado production--drug cartels such as the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) have muscled into the trade, extorting growers, hijacking shipments, and murdering anyone who refuses to pay protection money, turning orchards into contested territory where "blood avocados" follow the same brutal logic as conflict minerals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab471f8d-8ef1-44a5-80fc-6899df37fad6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Meanwhile, the legitimate side of the industry is scarcely less cutthroat: a handful of powerful packing associations and exporters dominate cross-border trade, controlling pricing from the orchard floor to the North American produce aisle while smaller farmers get squeezed by rising water costs, deforestation fines, and labor shortages. Because the United States depends on Mexican avocados for roughly 90 percent of its supply--and because Americans will still pay a premium for guacamole whether the price is eight dollars or twelve--the entire market operates as a vertically integrated pressure cooker where cartels extort the margins, middlemen fix the prices, and the only thing more abundant than the fruit itself is the body count.
So with that in mind...
Let's start with Primal Kitchen. Ring a bell? Beautiful branding. Looks like it was designed by a caveman who got an MBA at Stanford. Lots of pictures of avocados dressed like they're about to give a TED Talk. Kraft Heinz--you know, the Empire of Ketchup, the Sultan of Squirtable Mustard, the conglomerate that brought you mac and cheese in a box shaped like happiness--Kraft Heinz looked at Primal Kitchen and said, "Yes. That. We want that." And they bought it. For two hundred million dollars. Two. Hundred. Million.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72ec4fdd-34fe-4890-9891-b803b537965d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, when you spend that kind of money, you expect at least a participation trophy. You expect maybe a warehouse full of *actual* avocados. What you do not expect is to wake up the next morning to a headline that says a UC Davis study found ninety percent of their avocado oil products are about as authentic as my grandmother's natural hair color.
**[SMALL MUSIC STING]**
Ninety percent! That's not a margin of error. That's not "whoops, one batch got mixed up." That's an institutional commitment to fibbing. If you buy a lottery ticket and have a ninety percent chance of *not* getting avocado oil, that's not food anymore--that's gambling. Primal Kitchen should come with a warning label: "May contain traces of reality."
But here's where it gets good. UC Davis--they're the scientists, the ones in lab coats doing the Lord's work while the rest of us are just trying to figure out if our sourdough starter is dead--they ran tests. And they found that ninety-three percent of the *chips* had no avocado oil. Despite the label saying, right there on the bag, "Made with Avocado Oil." Ninety-three percent. That means if you bought a bag of these chips and poured them into a bowl at your Super Bowl party, statistically speaking, the only thing in that bowl that contained avocado oil was the guilt you felt for eating them.
But folks, the dressings. Oh, *the dressings.*
**[BEAT]**
One. Hundred. Percent.
One hundred percent of the dressings came back with no avocado oil. None. Zero. The big bagel. That is not a failure rate; that is a perfect score in the wrong direction. It's like showing up to a calculus exam, writing "avocado" for every answer, and somehow getting expelled. Every. Single. Dressing. Ranch, Caesar, that spicy one with the picture of a pepper looking disappointed--it was all, allegedly, a gorgeous pageant of lies. The label says "avocado oil," the bottle says "avocado oil," your receipt says "avocado oil," but the contents say, "Surprise! It's probably soybean oil wearing aviator sunglasses and a fake mustache."
**[LAUGH TRACK / HOST CHUCKLE]**
Forty-eight out of fifty-four samples were inconsistent with avocado oil. Inconsistent. That's such a polite science word, isn't it? "Inconsistent." Like calling a bank robbery an "unauthorized withdrawal." No, no, no. These bottles didn't just have *inconsistent* oil. They had *imposter* oil. They had oil that looked at avocado oil on the shelf and said, "I can do that," with the confidence of a man at karaoke who only knows half the words.
And it wasn't just Primal Kitchen! This was industry-wide. Other brands failed at a rate of ninety-three percent for chips, one hundred percent for dressings, and seventy-one percent for mayonnaise. Seventy-one percent for mayo! Even the fraud is part-time! It's like the mayonnaise said, "You know what, some weeks I feel like being avocado oil, some weeks I feel like being refined sunflower oil with something to prove." At least the mayo had the decency to be only *mostly* fake. The dressings went full method actor. They committed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/55cc483f-ade2-4f75-af2d-9b05ebc225b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[MUSIC STING]**
So what is actually in there? Great question. I'm not a food scientist, but I've seen enough true crime to know that when someone's pretending to be something they're not, there's usually a cheaper, seedier replacement hiding in the basement. The study suggests a lot of these bottles are filled with cheaper refined oils--your soy, your canola, maybe some sunflower oil that got lost on the way to the bird feeder. And you, my friend, the health-conscious consumer who traded your beloved ranch for the "clean label" version, you are out here paying a premium price for what is essentially vegetable oil in a yoga outfit.
And let's talk about that premium price, because this is where it really stings. Avocado oil is expensive. It's the caviar of the Fry Daddy. You buy it because you want to believe you're doing something good for your body. You bring it home and display it on the counter like a trophy. "Look at me," the bottle says. "I am nourished." And Kraft Heinz looked at that psychology and said, "We'll take two hundred million dollars' worth of that self-esteem, please."
This is the health halo in full effect. You slap the word "avocado" on something, and suddenly it's not junk food; it's a *lifestyle*. It's not mayo; it's *clean* mayo. But apparently, clean is just a marketing term, like "artisan" or "hand-crafted" or "farm-to-table" when the farm is actually a chemical plant in New Jersey.
**[BEAT]**
I keep imagining the board meeting when Kraft Heinz bought Primal Kitchen. Some guy in a suit is standing in front of a PowerPoint, and the last slide just says: "Synergies." And someone raises a hand and asks, "But is there actually avocado oil in the bottles?" And the presenter says, "That's not really a synergy question, Chad." And they all voted and now here we are.
And the FDA? Where are they? Oh, they're busy. They're out there making sure oat milk doesn't get too cocky about calling itself milk. They're regulating whether your sparkling water can claim to be "natural." Meanwhile, over in Oil World, it's the Wild West. It's a snake-oil convention, except the snake oil is also fake. It's someone selling you a golden retriever and handing you a possum in a wig.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d66906a1-4a0a-4377-8dd7-5b8d7e4d72fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You know what's wild? If you walked into a store and tried to sell bottles labeled "Unicorn Tears," the FDA would shut you down unless you could prove the unicorn was real and depressed. But apparently, you can sell "100% Avocado Oil" and just... not. It's not regulated. It's not really checked. It's the honor system, and we have established that these companies have no honor. They have marketing budgets. They have dark glass bottles with elegant serif fonts. They have the audacity.
And--and!--the real kicker in all this is that the actual, legitimate avocado oil producers are getting screwed too. Imagine you're farmer Bob in California, and you actually squeeze avocados for a living, and now no one believes you because everybody else is running a juice scam. You're out there pressing avocados like a romantic poet, and meanwhile, some corporate giant is selling canola oil with a picture of your fruit on it. That's identity theft for produce.
Let's look at those numbers again because they're almost poetic. Forty-eight out of fifty-four samples. That's like if you ordered a dozen eggs and six of them were golf balls. Sure, they're round and white, but your morning is about to go sideways real fast. One hundred percent of dressings failed. If UC Davis had tested my dating profile in college, the results would have been similar: externally labeled as "emotionally available," internally found to be one hundred percent inconsistent.
**[SFX: SMALL RIMSHOT]**
And the mayonnaise. Seventy-one percent failure rate. That means twenty-nine percent of the mayo actually had avocado oil! Which makes me wonder if that twenty-nine percent was just a clerical error. Like someone in the factory was supposed to hit "soybean" and accidentally hit "actual avocado" and then got fired for exceeding expectations. "We don't DO that here, Gary! Pour it out!"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cc71b1a8-5a46-42f2-9532-a193ac46148f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, I know what the lawyers are prepping right now. "We stand by the quality of our--" yeah, yeah. Save it. You stood by the label, which claims one thing, and the chromatography says another. For those of us who didn't major in chemistry, chromatography is that thing scientists do where they shoot lasers or lasers-adjacent science at a substance and it tells them exactly what it is. And when UC Davis pointed their science stick at Primal Kitchen products, the science stick said, "That's not avocado; that's a costume."
I picture the scientists in the lab, holding up a beaker, squinting. "Hmm. This molecule is wearing Crocs and calling itself California cool. Suspicious."
And the chips. Ninety-three percent. So if you ate a bag of those chips and you thought you were being healthy, you were actually just eating lies with sea salt. You were crunching on deception. You were dipping into a bag of false consciousness while watching *The Bachelor*. The bag should just say, "Made with the *idea* of Avocado Oil." Or "Spiritually Inspired by Avocado." Or "Avocado Oil in the same way that I am spiritually a millionaire."
**[BEAT]**
This whole thing is just the latest chapter in America's ongoing quest to eat healthy without actually doing any work. We want the virtue. We want the Instagram story. We want to hold the bottle and feel like we've outsmarted death. And corporations show up like carnival barkers and say, "Step right up! For only eleven ninety-nine, you can purchase a feeling!" And we do it! We buy the feeling! We drizzle the feeling on a salad! And the feeling turns out to be processed seed oil and vibes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4568f41a-0293-4730-8295-203f5dc2f2f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You know what the solution is? Buy an avocado. A real one. It's shaped like a grenade and feels like a handshake from the earth. Cut it open. It's green inside. That's how you know. If your "avocado oil" isn't green and the bottle has been sitting on a shelf for fourteen months, ask yourself: where did the green go? Did it ascend to heaven? No. It was never there.
Make your own dressing. I know, I know, nobody wants to hear that. We want convenience. But it's literally oil and vinegar and a pinch of whatever your heart desires. You can do it. You're an adult. You pay taxes. You can emulsify.
**[MUSIC STING]**
I do want to take a quick second to salute the six products that passed. Six out of fifty-four. The valedictorians of honesty. The kids who did the homework while everyone else was cheating off each other. You've got to imagine those six bottles sitting in the pantry like, "Why does nobody pick us? We actually have avocado oil!" And the consumer is like, "You're too expensive and your label isn't pretty enough." That's the tragedy, people. The good guys finish last, and the soybean oil gets the shelf space.
And finally, Kraft Heinz. Two hundred million dollars. For this. For a brand that UC Davis just reduced to a meme. It's not even a food company anymore; it's an art installation about late-stage capitalism. They bought the façade. They bought the lie. They bought the caveman aesthetic. And now they own a study that says, essentially, "Your premium acquisition is a chemistry set of broken promises."
But hey, they still have ketchup. Ketchup doesn't lie. Ketchup is tomatoes and courage. Ketchup is honest. Stay in your lane, Heinz.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c91d9ab9-4549-4e2a-b3f2-406902e3b37e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So here's my advice: next time you're in the grocery store and you see a bottle of something promising you liquid health in a beautiful package, just remember--trust but verify. And if you can't verify it yourself with a mass spectrometer and a graduate degree, maybe just eat the actual fruit. The worst thing that can happen with a real avocado is it goes brown faster than your retirement plans. But at least it was real.
I'm going to leave you with this. The food industry is basically a magician: look at this hand, the one holding the words "All Natural," while the other hand is stuffing soybean oil into the bottle. And we are the audience, standing there with our mouths open, holding expired coupons for wellness.
Thanks for listening. I'll be back after the break. Try not to dress your salad with existential dread. It's fat-free, but it tastes like disappointment. And make your own guac...it's easy.
You've been listening to Steve A. and 'America the beautiful' on Nashville's Supertalk 99.7 WTN, Talk radio 102.3 Chattanooga and News talk 92.5FM/770AM WVNN Huntsville Alabama. Love y'all. Thanks for sticking around.

Avocados, the mob and a dark side of health food industry | | | Sep 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | (RADIO MONOLOGUE) [THEME MUSIC FADES UNDER] Okay, settle in, folks. Grab your artisanal popcorn--actually, wait. Check the bag first. Make sure it actually contains popcorn and not, say, just shredded wheat with ambition. Because we need to talk about avocado oil. The miracle elixir. The darling of every health podcast, every paleo CrossFit mom, every guy in your office who brings a salad in a glass container and makes you feel bad about your sandwich. We were told it was good fat. We were told it was worth twelve dollars a bottle. We were told... a lot of things. Turns out, we were told lies. Quick side note: Avocados have earned the nickname "green gold" because the dense, creamy fruit generates profit margins that rival precious metals, but beneath the glossy piles of Hass avocados at your neighborhood grocery lies a supply chain increasingly shaped by cartel violence and monopoly control. In Michoacan, Mexico--the heart of global avocado production--drug cartels such as the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) have muscled into the trade, extorting growers, hijacking shipments, and murdering anyone who refuses to pay protection money, turning orchards into contested territory where "blood avocados" follow the same brutal logic as conflict minerals. | | ---|---|--- Meanwhile, the legitimate side of the industry is scarcely less cutthroat: a handful of powerful packing associations and exporters dominate cross-border trade, controlling pricing from the orchard floor to the North American produce aisle while smaller farmers get squeezed by rising water costs, deforestation fines, and labor shortages. Because the United States depends on Mexican avocados for roughly 90 percent of its supply--and because Americans will still pay a premium for guacamole whether the price is eight dollars or twelve--the entire market operates as a vertically integrated pressure cooker where cartels extort the margins, middlemen fix the prices, and the only thing more abundant than the fruit itself is the body count. So with that in mind... Let's start with Primal Kitchen. Ring a bell? Beautiful branding. Looks like it was designed by a caveman who got an MBA at Stanford. Lots of pictures of avocados dressed like they're about to give a TED Talk. Kraft Heinz--you know, the Empire of Ketchup, the Sultan of Squirtable Mustard, the conglomerate that brought you mac and cheese in a box shaped like happiness--Kraft Heinz looked at Primal Kitchen and said, "Yes. That. We want that." And they bought it. For two hundred million dollars. Two. Hundred. Million. | | ---|---|--- Now, when you spend that kind of money, you expect at least a participation trophy. You expect maybe a warehouse full of actual avocados. What you do not expect is to wake up the next morning to a headline that says a UC Davis study found ninety percent of their avocado oil products are about as authentic as my grandmother's natural hair color. [SMALL MUSIC STING] Ninety percent! That's not a margin of error. That's not "whoops, one batch got mixed up." That's an institutional commitment to fibbing. If you buy a lottery ticket and have a ninety percent chance of not getting avocado oil, that's not food anymore--that's gambling. Primal Kitchen should come with a warning label: "May contain traces of reality." But here's where it gets good. UC Davis--they're the scientists, the ones in lab coats doing the Lord's work while the rest of us are just trying to figure out if our sourdough starter is dead--they ran tests. And they found that ninety-three percent of the chips had no avocado oil. Despite the label saying, right there on the bag, "Made with Avocado Oil." Ninety-three percent. That means if you bought a bag of these chips and poured them into a bowl at your Super Bowl party, statistically speaking, the only thing in that bowl that contained avocado oil was the guilt you felt for eating them. But folks, the dressings. Oh, the dressings. [BEAT] One. Hundred. Percent. One hundred percent of the dressings came back with no avocado oil. None. Zero. The big bagel. That is not a failure rate; that is a perfect score in the wrong direction. It's like showing up to a calculus exam, writing "avocado" for every answer, and somehow getting expelled. Every. Single. Dressing. Ranch, Caesar, that spicy one with the picture of a pepper looking disappointed--it was all, allegedly, a gorgeous pageant of lies. The label says "avocado oil," the bottle says "avocado oil," your receipt says "avocado oil," but the contents say, "Surprise! It's probably soybean oil wearing aviator sunglasses and a fake mustache." [LAUGH TRACK / HOST CHUCKLE] Forty-eight out of fifty-four samples were inconsistent with avocado oil. Inconsistent. That's such a polite science word, isn't it? "Inconsistent." Like calling a bank robbery an "unauthorized withdrawal." No, no, no. These bottles didn't just have inconsistent oil. They had imposter oil. They had oil that looked at avocado oil on the shelf and said, "I can do that," with the confidence of a man at karaoke who only knows half the words. And it wasn't just Primal Kitchen! This was industry-wide. Other brands failed at a rate of ninety-three percent for chips, one hundred percent for dressings, and seventy-one percent for mayonnaise. Seventy-one percent for mayo! Even the fraud is part-time! It's like the mayonnaise said, "You know what, some weeks I feel like being avocado oil, some weeks I feel like being refined sunflower oil with something to prove." At least the mayo had the decency to be only mostly fake. The dressings went full method actor. They committed. | | ---|---|--- [MUSIC STING] So what is actually in there? Great question. I'm not a food scientist, but I've seen enough true crime to know that when someone's pretending to be something they're not, there's usually a cheaper, seedier replacement hiding in the basement. The study suggests a lot of these bottles are filled with cheaper refined oils--your soy, your canola, maybe some sunflower oil that got lost on the way to the bird feeder. And you, my friend, the health-conscious consumer who traded your beloved ranch for the "clean label" version, you are out here paying a premium price for what is essentially vegetable oil in a yoga outfit. And let's talk about that premium price, because this is where it really stings. Avocado oil is expensive. It's the caviar of the Fry Daddy. You buy it because you want to believe you're doing something good for your body. You bring it home and display it on the counter like a trophy. "Look at me," the bottle says. "I am nourished." And Kraft Heinz looked at that psychology and said, "We'll take two hundred million dollars' worth of that self-esteem, please." This is the health halo in full effect. You slap the word "avocado" on something, and suddenly it's not junk food; it's a lifestyle. It's not mayo; it's clean mayo. But apparently, clean is just a marketing term, like "artisan" or "hand-crafted" or "farm-to-table" when the farm is actually a chemical plant in New Jersey. [BEAT] I keep imagining the board meeting when Kraft Heinz bought Primal Kitchen. Some guy in a suit is standing in front of a PowerPoint, and the last slide just says: "Synergies." And someone raises a hand and asks, "But is there actually avocado oil in the bottles?" And the presenter says, "That's not really a synergy question, Chad." And they all voted and now here we are. And the FDA? Where are they? Oh, they're busy. They're out there making sure oat milk doesn't get too cocky about calling itself milk. They're regulating whether your sparkling water can claim to be "natural." Meanwhile, over in Oil World, it's the Wild West. It's a snake-oil convention, except the snake oil is also fake. It's someone selling you a golden retriever and handing you a possum in a wig. | | ---|---|--- You know what's wild? If you walked into a store and tried to sell bottles labeled "Unicorn Tears," the FDA would shut you down unless you could prove the unicorn was real and depressed. But apparently, you can sell "100% Avocado Oil" and just... not. It's not regulated. It's not really checked. It's the honor system, and we have established that these companies have no honor. They have marketing budgets. They have dark glass bottles with elegant serif fonts. They have the audacity. And--and!--the real kicker in all this is that the actual, legitimate avocado oil producers are getting screwed too. Imagine you're farmer Bob in California, and you actually squeeze avocados for a living, and now no one believes you because everybody else is running a juice scam. You're out there pressing avocados like a romantic poet, and meanwhile, some corporate giant is selling canola oil with a picture of your fruit on it. That's identity theft for produce. Let's look at those numbers again because they're almost poetic. Forty-eight out of fifty-four samples. That's like if you ordered a dozen eggs and six of them were golf balls. Sure, they're round and white, but your morning is about to go sideways real fast. One hundred percent of dressings failed. If UC Davis had tested my dating profile in college, the results would have been similar: externally labeled as "emotionally available," internally found to be one hundred percent inconsistent. [SFX: SMALL RIMSHOT] And the mayonnaise. Seventy-one percent failure rate. That means twenty-nine percent of the mayo actually had avocado oil! Which makes me wonder if that twenty-nine percent was just a clerical error. Like someone in the factory was supposed to hit "soybean" and accidentally hit "actual avocado" and then got fired for exceeding expectations. "We don't DO that here, Gary! Pour it out!" | | ---|---|--- Now, I know what the lawyers are prepping right now. "We stand by the quality of our--" yeah, yeah. Save it. You stood by the label, which claims one thing, and the chromatography says another. For those of us who didn't major in chemistry, chromatography is that thing scientists do where they shoot lasers or lasers-adjacent science at a substance and it tells them exactly what it is. And when UC Davis pointed their science stick at Primal Kitchen products, the science stick said, "That's not avocado; that's a costume." I picture the scientists in the lab, holding up a beaker, squinting. "Hmm. This molecule is wearing Crocs and calling itself California cool. Suspicious." And the chips. Ninety-three percent. So if you ate a bag of those chips and you thought you were being healthy, you were actually just eating lies with sea salt. You were crunching on deception. You were dipping into a bag of false consciousness while watching The Bachelor. The bag should just say, "Made with the idea of Avocado Oil." Or "Spiritually Inspired by Avocado." Or "Avocado Oil in the same way that I am spiritually a millionaire." [BEAT] This whole thing is just the latest chapter in America's ongoing quest to eat healthy without actually doing any work. We want the virtue. We want the Instagram story. We want to hold the bottle and feel like we've outsmarted death. And corporations show up like carnival barkers and say, "Step right up! For only eleven ninety-nine, you can purchase a feeling!" And we do it! We buy the feeling! We drizzle the feeling on a salad! And the feeling turns out to be processed seed oil and vibes. | | ---|---|--- You know what the solution is? Buy an avocado. A real one. It's shaped like a grenade and feels like a handshake from the earth. Cut it open. It's green inside. That's how you know. If your "avocado oil" isn't green and the bottle has been sitting on a shelf for fourteen months, ask yourself: where did the green go? Did it ascend to heaven? No. It was never there. Make your own dressing. I know, I know, nobody wants to hear that. We want convenience. But it's literally oil and vinegar and a pinch of whatever your heart desires. You can do it. You're an adult. You pay taxes. You can emulsify. [MUSIC STING] I do want to take a quick second to salute the six products that passed. Six out of fifty-four. The valedictorians of honesty. The kids who did the homework while everyone else was cheating off each other. You've got to imagine those six bottles sitting in the pantry like, "Why does nobody pick us? We actually have avocado oil!" And the consumer is like, "You're too expensive and your label isn't pretty enough." That's the tragedy, people. The good guys finish last, and the soybean oil gets the shelf space. And finally, Kraft Heinz. Two hundred million dollars. For this. For a brand that UC Davis just reduced to a meme. It's not even a food company anymore; it's an art installation about late-stage capitalism. They bought the façade. They bought the lie. They bought the caveman aesthetic. And now they own a study that says, essentially, "Your premium acquisition is a chemistry set of broken promises." But hey, they still have ketchup. Ketchup doesn't lie. Ketchup is tomatoes and courage. Ketchup is honest. Stay in your lane, Heinz. | | ---|---|--- So here's my advice: next time you're in the grocery store and you see a bottle of something promising you liquid health in a beautiful package, just remember--trust but verify. And if you can't verify it yourself with a mass spectrometer and a graduate degree, maybe just eat the actual fruit. The worst thing that can happen with a real avocado is it goes brown faster than your retirement plans. But at least it was real. I'm going to leave you with this. The food industry is basically a magician: look at this hand, the one holding the words "All Natural," while the other hand is stuffing soybean oil into the bottle. And we are the audience, standing there with our mouths open, holding expired coupons for wellness. Thanks for listening. I'll be back after the break. A U.S. Postal Service official filed a whistleblower report that was published recently, **alleging that the agency was moving forward with a “ _secretive, rushed_ ” effort to carry out an executive order exerting federal control over mail voting**, despite a court order blocking those plans. Until just a few weeks ago, appointees at the Postal Service were still pushing forward to implement rules on mail-in voting that would put Americans’ ability to cast a mail-in ballot into jeopardy.The report asserts "_that the “**risky and haphazard** ” implementation of [the executive] order could lead to a “**catastrophic failure** ” in the mail ballot system ahead of this year’s midterm elections._"The report also says that USPS had been planning to complete a system, known as the Federal Ballot Mail Portal, which would serve as a **database for voter information that could be used to reject ballots**. The report claims the target date for that new portal to go into service was September 1st. Now they've re-focused on the 2028 election instead. **[Team, this report was a chilling look inside the suppressive plan to ignore court orders and subvert the Constitution. | | | More from the whistleblower report: The USPS official, describing their work on the portal, raised “ _grave concerns_ ” that **the portal’s verification process could reject tens of thousands of ballots in a bulk-mailing batch** if “ _even one bar code on one single ballot_ ” failed to properly scan, and that the rushed, “ _slapdash_ ” development of the portal would **significantly increase the chance of errors and other failures in the verification process**.
